⏺ Now I have a thorough picture of what exists. Here's my analysis and a proposed design:                      
                                                                                                                
  ---                                                                                                           
  What Already Exists                                                                                           
                                                                                                                
  The project already has solid pieces:                                                                         
  - simulation/ — entry/exit logic (4h RSI entries, 5m MFE-ladder replay)                                       
  - study/ — exploratory market research scripts                                                                
  - scripts/ — CLI runners that orchestrate full backtests                                                      
  - runs/ — timestamped run artifacts (webapp auto-discovers these)                                             
  - webapp/ — React dashboard that reads runs + candle DB                                                       
                                                                                                                
  The gap is: no standard contract for what a "strategy" or "study" looks like, so each new script is one-off   
  and the webapp can't generically consume new work.                                                            
                                                                                                                
  ---                                                                                                           
  Proposed Design: playground/ folder
                                     
  Rather than modifying the existing simulation code (which works), create a new playground/ folder that wraps
  it with standards. Existing scripts keep running as-is.                                                       
   
  playground/                                                                                                   
  ├── base/       
  │   ├── strategy.py        # Abstract base class for any strategy
  │   ├── study.py           # Abstract base class for any study
  │   ├── schemas.py         # Standard dataclasses (Trade, StudyResult, RunManifest)
  │   └── sim_rules.py       # Documented simulation assumptions/rules                                          
  ├── engine/                                                                                                   
  │   ├── candle_sim.py      # Standard sim engine (enforces rules)                                             
  │   └── run_writer.py      # Writes outputs in webapp-compatible run format                                   
  ├── strategies/            # Agent-created strategies go here                                                 
  │   └── _example/          # Reference implementation                                                         
  └── studies/               # Agent-created studies go here                                                    
      └── _example/          # Reference implementation
                                                                                                                
  ---             
  The Three Standards
                                                                                                                
  1. Simulation Rules (sim_rules.py)
                                                                                                                
  Codified assumptions so any agent knows what is and isn't valid:                                              
  - Entries only on bar close (no look-ahead)
  - Fills at open of next bar (configurable slippage offset)                                                    
  - Round-trip fee in bps (must be declared)                
  - No partial fills — full fill assumed                                                                        
  - SL/TP checked against candle high/low (not tick data — worst-case resolution)                               
  - One position per asset at a time                                                                            
                                                                                                                
  2. Study Standard (BaseStudy)
                                                                                                                
  Every study must produce:                                                                                     
  study_output/
    manifest.json     # name, version, assets, timeframe, date range, run_ts                                    
    summary.json      # key metrics dict                                    
    events.csv        # raw event rows (standardized columns)                                                   
    README.md         # auto-generated from docstring + summary                                                 
                                                                                                                
  3. Strategy/Simulation Standard (BaseStrategy + RunWriter)                                                    
                                                                                                                
  Every simulation writes to runs/ in the existing format the webapp already reads, plus a manifest.json the    
  webapp can use to label/filter runs:                                                                          
  runs/run_<name>_<ts>/                                                                                         
    manifest.json     # strategy name, params, assumptions declared
    artifacts/                                                     
      summary.csv     # per-chunk metrics (same schema as existing)                                             
      metrics.json    # aggregate stats                            
    trades/                                                                                                     
      <ASSET>.csv     # per-asset trade ledger (same schema as existing)                                        
   
  ---                                                                                                           
  Options to Proceed
                                                                                                                
  A. Create playground/ now — build the base classes, schemas, sim rules, and one reference strategy that wraps
  the existing RSI sim. Clean separation, existing code untouched.                                              
   
  B. Audit first — I read the existing simulation/ and study/ files in detail, then we decide exactly what to   
  copy vs. refactor before writing anything.
                                                                                                                
  C. Minimal MVP — just schemas.py + sim_rules.py as a written contract (no classes yet), plus a run_writer.py  
  that any script can call to emit webapp-compatible output.
                                                                                                                
  Which direction fits best, and do the simulation rules I listed match your assumptions? Any I'm missing (e.g.,
   how you handle the case where SL and TP are both hit in the same bar)?

⏺ Now I have everything I need. Let me compile the full picture.
                                                                                                                
  ---                                                                                                           
  Audit Findings                                                                                                
                                                                                                                
  What's solid and shouldn't be touched                                                                         
                                                                                                                
  - simulation/ltf_trade_management_study.py — the ReplayResult dataclass and replay_trade_mfe_ladder_5m() are  
  mature, well-commented, with documented assumptions. This is the best-written code in the project.            
  - run_config.json → runs/ folder structure already works as a contract the webapp reads.                      
  - The trade CSV schema (from the actual files) is already a de facto standard — the webapp's parseTradeCsv()  
  explicitly knows which fields are numeric.                                                                    
                                                                                                                
  Problems found (duplications & inconsistencies)                                                               
                  
  1. load_merged_5m is defined in scripts/massive_chunk_backtest_5m.py and duplicated in                        
  massive_chunk_backtest_5m_v1fix.py. Every study file imports it from a script:
  from massive_chunk_backtest_5m_v1fix import load_merged_5m  # in study/*.py                                   
  Studies importing from scripts is backwards — utilities should flow the other way.
                                                                                                                
  2. wilder_atr() is copy-pasted verbatim in both study/atr_random_entry_study.py and                           
  study/xrp_fvg_regime_concepts_study.py.                                                                       
                                                                                                                
  3. _fee_r() and ReplayResult are duplicated between ltf_trade_management_study.py and                         
  ltf_trade_management_study_v1fix.py (v1fix appears to be a near-copy of the original).
                                                                                                                
  4. No study has standardized output. Some print to stdout, some write CSVs to study/out/, some write nowhere. 
  There's no manifest.json or summary schema.
                                                                                                                
  5. Webapp has a hardcoded trade file regex:
  /^trade_details_(v1fix|v1)_(tp[0-9p]+)\.csv$/i
  Any new strategy that doesn't name its files trade_details_v1_tp*.csv will be invisible to the webapp.        
                                                                                                        
  6. run_config.json schema is implicit — no validation, no documented required fields. The webapp silently     
  fails if it's missing.                                                                                        
                                                                                                                
  ---                                                                                                           
  The real simulation rules (extracted from code)
                                                 
  These are currently scattered in docstrings and comments — never written down in one place:
                                                                                                                
  ┌───────────────────┬──────────────────────────────────┬─────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ 
  │       Rule        │          Where it lives          │                     Detail                      │    
  ├──────────────────┼─────────────────────────────────┼────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
  │ Entry timing     │ run_simulation_trades L226-243  │ Bar i entry at open; signal fires when RSI[i-1]    │
  │                  │                                 │ crossed RSI[i-2]                                   │
  ├──────────────────┼─────────────────────────────────┼────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤   
  │ Stop placement   │ Same, L228/237                  │ Structural: min/max of sl_n bars ending at i-1     │
  ├──────────────────┼─────────────────────────────────┼────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤   
  │ Exit order (same │ ltf_study docstring L16-17      │ SL checked before TP before BE-arm (conservative)  │
  │  bar)            │                                 │                                                    │   
  ├──────────────────┼─────────────────────────────────┼────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤   
  │ Fill assumption  │ Implicit                        │ Full fill at next bar open; no partial fills       │
  │                  │                                 │ modeled                                            │   
  ├──────────────────┼─────────────────────────────────┼────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
  │ Fee model        │ _fee_r()                        │ entry_price * fee_bps / 10000 / risk — fee         │   
  │                  │                                 │ expressed in R                                     │   
  ├──────────────────┼─────────────────────────────────┼────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
  │ 5m stop deferred │ replay_trade_mfe_ladder_5m      │ Wick-touch queues new stop, activates at NEXT bar  │   
  │                  │ docstring                       │ open                                               │   
  ├──────────────────┼─────────────────────────────────┼────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
  │ Entry bucket     │ Same                            │ No management fills in entry 4h candle             │   
  │ skip             │                                 │ (skip_entry_bucket_hours=4.0)                      │   
  ├──────────────────┼─────────────────────────────────┼────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
  │ MFE cap          │ Same                            │ cap_lock_by_mfe=True — lock can't exceed actual    │   
  │                  │                                 │ MFE reached                                        │
  ├──────────────────┼─────────────────────────────────┼────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
  │ Same-bar SL+TP   │ Unhandled                       │ If both hit same bar, SL wins (conservative)       │
  └──────────────────┴─────────────────────────────────┴────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘   
   
  ---                                                                                                           
  Recommendation  

  Given all this, here's what makes sense:

  Step 1 — Fix the foundation first (small, non-breaking)                                                       
   
  Move load_merged_5m, wilder_atr, and build_4h_rsi into simulation/ as shared utilities. The study files'      
  imports break, but they're the ones that were wrong anyway. This doesn't touch any simulation logic.
                                                                                                                
  Step 2 — Create playground/                                                                                   
   
  playground/                                                                                                   
  ├── __init__.py 
  ├── sim_rules.py        # Written record of all assumptions above
  ├── schemas.py          # Dataclasses: TradeRecord, StudyManifest, RunManifest
  ├── base_study.py       # Abstract: run() → StudyResult, auto-writes manifest.json + events.csv               
  ├── base_strategy.py    # Abstract: generate_signals() + replay() → writes run folder                         
  └── run_writer.py       # Handles the runs/ folder structure + run_config.json format                         
                                                                                                                
  Step 3 — Update the webapp's file regex                                                                       
                                                                                                                
  Generalize index.cjs:116 from hardcoded v1fix|v1 to accept any trade_details_<name>_tp*.csv pattern, so new   
  strategies automatically appear.
                                                                                                                
  What NOT to touch

  - simulation/ltf_trade_management_study.py — leave intact, import from it                                     
  - scripts/massive_chunk_backtest_5m*.py — existing runs still work
  - runs/ folder structure — already correct, just formalize it                                                 
                                                                                                                
  ---                                                                                                           
  Does this match your intent? A few questions before I start:                                                  
                                                              
  1. ltf_trade_management_study_v1fix.py — is this meaningfully different from the original, or is it safe to
  consolidate? It appears to be a near-duplicate.                                                               
  2. Studies — should the standard study output go to study/out/ (current convention) or under runs/ alongside
  simulations? Or a separate study_runs/ folder?                                                                
  3. Webapp regex — are you ok with me updating index.cjs to accept a more general naming pattern, or do you
  want new playground strategies to match the existing v1/v1fix naming?

⏺ Good question — the existing webapp has real value (candlestick charts + trade overlays work well) but the    
  React+Node stack is a burden to maintain and agents can't contribute to it. Here's the honest comparison:

  ---                                                                                                           
  Option A: Keep the webapp
                                                                                                                
  Pros: TradingView-quality charts already work, 4h+5m overlay is built
  Cons: React+Node — agents can't write visualization code, hardcoded file patterns, requires running two       
  servers, hard to extend                                                                                       
                                                                                                                
  Option B: Replace with Streamlit                                                                              
                  
  Pros:
  - Pure Python — agents write strategy code AND visualization code in the same language
  - Reads your standardized CSVs/JSONs directly, no backend server                                              
  - streamlit-lightweight-charts gives the same TradingView-quality candlesticks
  - One command: streamlit run lab/app.py                                                                       
  - Each strategy/study can ship its own Streamlit page                                                         
  - Hot reload, easy to audit                                                                                   
                                                                                                                
  Cons: Slightly less polished than a custom React app, some layout constraints                                 
                                                                                                                
  Option C: Marimo notebooks                                                                                    
                                                                                                                
  Reactive Python notebooks that can run as webapps. Good but less ecosystem maturity than Streamlit.           
   
  ---                                                                                                           
  My recommendation: Streamlit
                              
  It's the right fit because the whole point is agents producing auditable outputs. If an agent writes a
  strategy, it also writes:                                                                                     
  1. The strategy logic (strategies/rsi_4h/strategy.py)
  2. The simulation output (runs/ CSVs)                                                                         
  3. A Streamlit page that visualizes it (strategies/rsi_4h/viz.py)
                                                                                                                
  The main lab/app.py is a dashboard that auto-discovers all runs and lets you drill into any of them — same
  concept as the existing webapp, but everything in Python.

⏺ Now I have a thorough picture of what exists. Here's my analysis and a proposed design:

  ---
  What Already Exists

  The project already has solid pieces:
  - simulation/ — entry/exit logic (4h RSI entries, 5m MFE-ladder replay)
  - study/ — exploratory market research scripts
  - scripts/ — CLI runners that orchestrate full backtests
  - runs/ — timestamped run artifacts (webapp auto-discovers these)
  - webapp/ — React dashboard that reads runs + candle DB

  The gap is: no standard contract for what a "strategy" or "study" looks like, so each new script is one-off
  and the webapp can't generically consume new work.

  ---
  Proposed Design: playground/ folder

  Rather than modifying the existing simulation code (which works), create a new playground/ folder that wraps
  it with standards. Existing scripts keep running as-is.

  playground/
  ├── base/
  │   ├── strategy.py        # Abstract base class for any strategy
  │   ├── study.py           # Abstract base class for any study
  │   ├── schemas.py         # Standard dataclasses (Trade, StudyResult, RunManifest)
  │   └── sim_rules.py       # Documented simulation assumptions/rules
  ├── engine/
  │   ├── candle_sim.py      # Standard sim engine (enforces rules)
  │   └── run_writer.py      # Writes outputs in webapp-compatible run format
  ├── strategies/            # Agent-created strategies go here
  │   └── _example/          # Reference implementation
  └── studies/               # Agent-created studies go here
      └── _example/          # Reference implementation

  ---
  The Three Standards

  1. Simulation Rules (sim_rules.py)

  Codified assumptions so any agent knows what is and isn't valid:
  - Entries only on bar close (no look-ahead)
  - Fills at open of next bar (configurable slippage offset)
  - Round-trip fee in bps (must be declared)
  - No partial fills — full fill assumed
  - SL/TP checked against candle high/low (not tick data — worst-case resolution)
  - One position per asset at a time

  2. Study Standard (BaseStudy)

  Every study must produce:
  study_output/
    manifest.json     # name, version, assets, timeframe, date range, run_ts
    summary.json      # key metrics dict
    events.csv        # raw event rows (standardized columns)
    README.md         # auto-generated from docstring + summary

  3. Strategy/Simulation Standard (BaseStrategy + RunWriter)

  Every simulation writes to runs/ in the existing format the webapp already reads, plus a manifest.json the
  webapp can use to label/filter runs:
  runs/run_<name>_<ts>/
    manifest.json     # strategy name, params, assumptions declared
    artifacts/
      summary.csv     # per-chunk metrics (same schema as existing)
      metrics.json    # aggregate stats
    trades/
      <ASSET>.csv     # per-asset trade ledger (same schema as existing)

  ---
  Options to Proceed

  A. Create playground/ now — build the base classes, schemas, sim rules, and one reference strategy that wraps
  the existing RSI sim. Clean separation, existing code untouched.

  B. Audit first — I read the existing simulation/ and study/ files in detail, then we decide exactly what to
  copy vs. refactor before writing anything.

  C. Minimal MVP — just schemas.py + sim_rules.py as a written contract (no classes yet), plus a run_writer.py
  that any script can call to emit webapp-compatible output.

  Which direction fits best, and do the simulation rules I listed match your assumptions? Any I'm missing (e.g.,
   how you handle the case where SL and TP are both hit in the same bar)?

  ---
  Audit Findings

  What's solid and shouldn't be touched

  - simulation/ltf_trade_management_study.py — the ReplayResult dataclass and replay_trade_mfe_ladder_5m() are

  - The trade CSV schema (from the actual files) is already a de facto standard — the webapp's parseTradeCsv()
  explicitly knows which fields are numeric.

  Problems found (duplications & inconsistencies)

  1. load_merged_5m is defined in scripts/massive_chunk_backtest_5m.py and duplicated in
  massive_chunk_backtest_5m_v1fix.py. Every study file imports it from a script:
  from massive_chunk_backtest_5m_v1fix import load_merged_5m  # in study/*.py
  Studies importing from scripts is backwards — utilities should flow the other way.

  2. wilder_atr() is copy-pasted verbatim in both study/atr_random_entry_study.py and
  study/xrp_fvg_regime_concepts_study.py.

  3. _fee_r() and ReplayResult are duplicated between ltf_trade_management_study.py and
  ltf_trade_management_study_v1fix.py (v1fix appears to be a near-copy of the original).

  4. No study has standardized output. Some print to stdout, some write CSVs to study/out/, some write nowhere.
  There's no manifest.json or summary schema.

  5. Webapp has a hardcoded trade file regex:
  /^trade_details_(v1fix|v1)_(tp[0-9p]+)\.csv$/i
  Any new strategy that doesn't name its files trade_details_v1_tp*.csv will be invisible to the webapp.

  6. run_config.json schema is implicit — no validation, no documented required fields. The webapp silently
  fails if it's missing.

  The real simulation rules (extracted from code)

  These are currently scattered in docstrings and comments — never written down in one place:

  playground/

  ├── base_study.py       # Abstract: run() → StudyResult, auto-writes manifest.json + events.csv

⏺ Good question — the existing webapp has real value (candlestick charts + trade overlays work well) but the
  React+Node stack is a burden to maintain and agents can't contribute to it. Here's the honest comparison:

  ---
  Option A: Keep the webapp

  Pros: TradingView-quality charts already work, 4h+5m overlay is built
  Cons: React+Node — agents can't write visualization code, hardcoded file patterns, requires running two
  servers, hard to extend

  Option B: Replace with Streamlit

  Pros:
  - Pure Python — agents write strategy code AND visualization code in the same language
  - Reads your standardized CSVs/JSONs directly, no backend server
  - streamlit-lightweight-charts gives the same TradingView-quality candlesticks
  - One command: streamlit run lab/app.py
  - Each strategy/study can ship its own Streamlit page
  - Hot reload, easy to audit

  Cons: Slightly less polished than a custom React app, some layout constraints

  Option C: Marimo notebooks

  Reactive Python notebooks that can run as webapps. Good but less ecosystem maturity than Streamlit.

  ---
  My recommendation: Streamlit

  It's the right fit because the whole point is agents producing auditable outputs. If an agent writes a
  strategy, it also writes:
  1. The strategy logic (strategies/rsi_4h/strategy.py)
  2. The simulation output (runs/ CSVs)
  3. A Streamlit page that visualizes it (strategies/rsi_4h/viz.py)

  The main lab/app.py is a dashboard that auto-discovers all runs and lets you drill into any of them — same
  concept as the existing webapp, but everything in Python.

  ---
  Shall I:
  1. Create the lab/ folder with the full structure
  2. Port the RSI 4h strategy in as the reference implementation
  3. Build a Streamlit app that replicates what the existing webapp does (trade list + 4h chart + 5m detail +
  equity curve)

  And we leave the existing webapp as-is (don't delete it, just stop developing it)?

⏺ Found both flaws. The differences are clear and specific. Let me document them before touching code.          
                                                                                                                
  ---                                                                                                           
  The two flaws in the original code (vs v1fix)                                                                 
                                                                                                                
  Flaw 1 — The big one: entry bar grace period                                                                  
                                                                                                                
  Original replay_trade_mfe_ladder_5m:                      
  skip_entry_bucket_hours: float = 4.0   # ← FLAW                                                               
  V1fix:                                                    
  skip_entry_bucket_hours: float = 0.0   # ← FIX                                                                
                                                
  With skip=4.0, SL and TP cannot fire during the 4h entry candle. The trade gets a 4h immunity window after    
  entry. In reality, your stop is live from the moment you enter. Many trades that would have immediately       
  reversed and stopped out in the entry bar were artificially kept alive — this is why results looked too good.
                                                                                                                
  Flaw 2 — Deferred stop updates                            

  Original uses pending_stop — when MFE triggers the lock level, the stop only moves at the next bar's open:    
  pending_stop = desired   # queued, not active yet
  V1fix applies the lock immediately in the same bar — the tighter stop can be hit by the same candle's adverse 
  wick. More realistic: in real trading, your stop-limit can be triggered the moment price reverses after       
  hitting the MFE level.                                                                                        
                                                                                                                
  Now fixing both in the lab:

       6  
       7 +  FLAW 1 (skip_entry_bucket_hours=4.0 default):                                                
       8 +    The original gave trades a 4h grace period after entry during which no SL                  
       9 +    or TP could fire. This artificially prevented many early stop-outs, making

      13 +  FLAW 2 (deferred stop updates):

      15 +    NEXT bar's open. This meant a whipsaw bar (price hits MFE then reverses)                   
      16 +    would not trigger the lock — the trade stayed open with the original stop.                 
      17 +    The fix (same-bar activation): when MFE threshold is hit, the tighter stop                 
      18 +    is live immediately and the same bar's adverse wick can hit it.

⏺ Good. Here's a summary of what was found and fixed:                                
                                                                                                                
  ---accept edits on (shift+tab to cycle) · esc to interrupt                                ◐ medium · /effort
  The two flaws, explained plainly                                                                              
                                                                                                                
  Flaw 1 — Entry bar grace period (skip=4.0)                                                                    
                                                                                                                
  The original code said "don't check for stops or exits for the first 4 hours after entry." In reality, the    
  moment you buy, your stop is placed. If price immediately reverses and hits your stop in the same 4h candle,  
  you're out. The original was preventing this, making trades survive adverse moves they wouldn't survive in    
  practice. This is the primary reason results looked too good.                                                 
                                                                                                                
  Flaw 2 — Deferred stop updates                                                                                
                                                                                                                
  When MFE triggered a tighter stop, the original queued it for the next bar. So if a 5m bar reached +1R and    
  immediately reversed to +0.8R (whipsaw), the trade continued unaffected because the lock wasn't live yet.     
  V1fix activates the lock in the same bar — if price touches +1R and reverses to +0.8R in the same candle, you 
  exit at +0.8R.                                                                                              

  Both are now fixed in lab/sim/exit.py and documented in lab/sim/rules.py (Rules 6 and 7) with the "why it     
  matters" explanation so any agent reading the rules understands the reasoning, not just the rule.

      108 +                                                                                              
      109 +═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════                   
      110 +SECTION E — STOP LOSS: PLACEMENT AND ACTIVATION                                               
      111 +═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════                   
      112 +                                                                                              
      113 +RULE 6 — The stop is live from the FIRST 5m bar at or after the entry time.                   
      114 +                                                                                              
      115 +  CORRECT:  first management bar = df5.loc[df5.index >= entry_ts]                             
      116 +  WRONG:    first management bar = df5.loc[df5.index >= entry_ts + 4h]                        
      117 +                                                                                              
      118 +The original code in this project used skip=4.0 (a 4h grace period). This                     
      119 +was a bug: it prevented stop-outs during the entry 4h candle, which inflated                  
      120 +results significantly. The stop order is live the moment you place it.                        
      121 +                                                                                              
      122 +When skip > 0 is acceptable:                                                                  
      123 +  - You are explicitly modeling a delayed stop placement (manual trading lag)                 
      124 +  - You set skip = your estimated lag in hours and document it                                
      125 +  - Default must always be 0.0                                                                
      126 +                                                                                              
      127 +RULE 7 — Exit at the STOP PRICE, not at the candle's extreme.                                 
      128 +                                                                                              
      129 +If your stop is at 20,100 and the bar's low reaches 20,000, you exit at                       
      130 +20,100 — your stop order fills at your stop price (assuming liquid market).                   
      131 +The simulation already does this correctly (it computes R from stop price,                    
      132 +not from bar low). Do not change this logic.                                                  
      133 +                                                                                              
      134 +Exception: gap-downs through a stop. For crypto 24/7 data, this is rare.                      
      135 +If you want to model gap fills, add a gap_slippage parameter explicitly.                      
      136 +                                                                                              
      137 +═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════                   
      138 +SECTION F — TAKE PROFIT: PLACEMENT AND FILL                                                   
      139 +═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════                   
      140 +                                                                                              
      141 +RULE 8 — TP is hit when the bar's High (long) or Low (short) reaches the TP                   
      142 +price. Fill at TP price, not beyond it.                                                       
      143 +                                                                                              
      144 +  Long TP hit:  bar.high >= tp_price → exit at tp_price                                       
      145 +  Short TP hit: bar.low  <= tp_price → exit at tp_price                                       
      146 +                                                                                              
      147 +Do not fill at bar.high — that would assume you got filled at the extreme,                    
      148 +which overstates profits.                                                                     
      149 +                                                                                              
      150 +═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════                   
      151 +SECTION G — SAME-BAR AMBIGUITY: SL AND TP BOTH HIT                                            
      152 +═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════                   
      153 +                                                                                              
      154 +RULE 9 — When both SL and TP are reachable within the same bar, SL wins.                      
      155 +                                                                                              
      156 +  Long:  bar.low <= SL and bar.high >= TP → exit at SL (conservative)                         
      157 +  Short: bar.high >= SL and bar.low <= TP → exit at SL (conservative)                         
      158 +                                                                                              
      159 +This is the conservative assumption: when we don't know the intrabar order,                   
      160 +we assume the adverse move came first. This slightly penalizes the strategy                   
      161 +vs optimistic assumptions, which is the correct direction for avoiding                        
      162 +overfitted results.                                                                           
      163 +                                                                                              
      164 +Bar-level exit check order (within each 5m bar):                                              
      165 +  1. Check SL                                                                                 
      166 +  2. If not stopped: check TP                                                                 
      167 +  3. If not exited: check MFE ladder triggers, update stop                                    
      168 +  4. If stop moved: check if new stop is immediately hit (same-bar activation)                
      169 +                                                                                              
      170 +For longs: check low before high.                                                             
      171 +For shorts: check high before low.                                                            
      172 +                                                                                              
      173 +═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════                   
      174 +SECTION H — TRADE MANAGEMENT: MFE LADDER AND STOP UPDATES                                     
      175 +═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════                   
      176 +                                                                                              
      177 +RULE 10 — MFE (Maximum Favorable Excursion) is tracked cumulatively from                      
      178 +entry. MFE is expressed in R-units: mfe_r = (peak_price - entry) / risk.                      
      179 +                                                                                              
      180 +RULE 11 — When an MFE threshold triggers a stop update, the new stop is                       
      181 +active IMMEDIATELY in the same bar (same-bar activation).                                     
      182 +                                                                                              
      183 +  CORRECT (same-bar):                                                                         
      184 +    bar.high >= entry + mfe_r * risk                                                          
      185 +    → update stop to entry + lock_r * risk                                                    
      186 +    → check if bar.low <= new stop in the SAME bar                                            
      187 +    → if yes: exit at new stop price                                                          
      188 +                                                                                              
      189 +  WRONG (deferred, the original bug):                                                         
      190 +    bar.high >= mfe_r threshold                                                               
      191 +    → queue new stop for NEXT bar                                                             
      192 +    → bar can whipsaw without hitting new stop                                                
      193 +                                                                                              
      194 +WHY: In the original code, a whipsaw bar (price moves to +1R then drops to                    
      195 ++0.8R in the same 5m candle) would NOT trigger the lock — the stop only moved                 
      196 +at the next bar. This gave trades a free pass through whipsaw bars, inflating                 
      197 +managed R. Same-bar activation is more realistic: the lock fires when price                   
      198 +trades there, regardless of when in the bar it happened.                                      
      199 +                                                                                              
      200 +RULE 12 — MFE cap: lock level cannot exceed MFE actually reached.                             
      201 +                                                                                              
      202 +  lock_eff = min(lock_r, mfe_max_r)   ← cap_lock_by_mfe = True (default)                      
      203 +                                                                                              
      204 +You cannot lock in +0.8R if price has only moved +0.5R. The stop update                       
      205 +is: max(current_stop, entry + min(lock_r, mfe_max_r) * risk) for longs.                       
      206 +                                                                                              
      207 +WHY: Without this cap, a stage defined as (mfe=1.0R, lock=0.8R) would move                    
      208 +your stop to +0.8R even if the MFE was only 1.0R by 1 tick. With the cap,                     
      209 +lock_eff = min(0.8, 1.0) = 0.8R. In practice this rarely differs, but at                      
      210 +exactly the threshold it prevents an unrealistic exact-tick lock.                             
      211 +                                                                                              
      212 +═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════                   
      213 +SECTION I — FEE MODEL                                                                         
      214 +═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════                   
      215 +                                                                                              
      216 +RULE 13 — Fee is round-trip (entry + exit combined), expressed in R-units.                    
      217 +                                                                                              
      218 +  fee_r = entry_price * fee_bps / 10_000 / risk                                               
      219 +                                                                                              
      220 +This fee is subtracted from the gross R at the end of the trade.                              
      221 +Default: 3.0 bps RT. This is approximate for liquid crypto spot/perp markets.                 
      222 +                                                                                              
      223 +Deduct fee once per trade regardless of how many stop updates happened.                       
      224 +Fee does not change when the stop moves (we are not modeling re-hedging costs).               
      225 +                                                                                              
      226 +═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════                   
      227 +SECTION J — DATA SOURCE AND QUALITY                                                           
      228 +═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════                   
      229 +                                                                                              
      230 +RULE 14 — All 5m candles come from the shared SQLite DB via core/db.py.                       
      231 +Use load_merged_5m(db_path, symbol) — never query the DB directly in                          
      232 +strategy code. This ensures consistent deduplication across sessions.                         
      233 +                                                                                              
      234 +RULE 15 — Data coverage must be validated before a simulation run.                            
      235 +                                                                                              
      236 +Before running a strategy, check:                                                             
      237 +  - Symbol has data from at least start_utc                                                   
      238 +  - No large gaps (>= 2h of missing 5m bars) in the backtest window                           
      239 +  - Minimum bar count: at least sl_n + rsi_window + 10 bars in the HTF series                 
      240 +                                                                                              
      241 +Trades that start outside the validated data window must be excluded.                         
      242 +                                                                                              
      243 +RULE 16 — The backtest window is [start_utc, end_utc). Half-open interval.                    
      244 +Trades are assigned to time chunks by their EXIT timestamp, not entry.                        
      245 +                                                                                              
      246 +═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════                   
      247 +SECTION K — KNOWN OPTIMISMS (ACCEPTABLE TRADE-OFFS)                                           
      248 +═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════                   
      249 +                                                                                              
      250 +The following are known ways the simulation is still more favorable than                      
      251 +live trading. They are accepted trade-offs, not bugs. Document any that                       
      252 +significantly affect your strategy's edge.                                                    
      253 +                                                                                              
      254 +K1 — Zero slippage: fills assumed at exact open/SL/TP prices.                                 
      255 +     Real fills may be worse, especially in fast markets.                                     
      256 +                                                                                              
      257 +K2 — Infinite liquidity: full fill assumed at all levels.                                     
      258 +     Real fills may be partial for large sizes or at illiquid levels.                         
      259 +                                                                                              
      260 +K3 — Bid/ask spread not modeled: fee_bps approximates this but                                
      261 +     spread can be higher in volatile periods.                                                
      262 +                                                                                              
      263 +K4 — Bar high/low order unknown: we assume conservative order (adverse first)                 
      264 +     but sometimes the favorable move does come first in reality.                             
      265 +                                                                                              
      266 +K5 — No funding rate (for perpetual futures strategies): if modeling perps,                   
      267 +     funding must be added as a periodic cost.                                                
      268 +                                                                                              
      269 +K6 — 5m bar resolution: intrabar path is unknown. Events that happen                          
      270 +     between 5m bar opens cannot be modeled. Tight stops near the entry                       
      271 +     price may produce different results in reality than in simulation.                       
      272 +                                                                                              
      273 +═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════                   
      274 +SECTION L — COMMON BUGS TO AVOID                                                              
      275 +═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════                   
      276 +                                                                                              
      277 +L1 — Using bar i's close to both generate a signal AND enter at bar i.                        
      278 +     Fix: signal at close[i-1] → entry at open[i].                                            
      279 +                                                                                              
      280 +L2 — Using bar i's high/low in the structural stop when entering at open[i].                  
      281 +     Fix: stop = min(low[i-sl_n : i]) — slice ends before i (not i+1).                        
      282 +                                                                                              
      283 +L3 — Starting the 5m replay after the 4h entry candle (skip=4h).                              
      284 +     Fix: skip_entry_bucket_hours=0.0. Stop is live from entry.                               
      285 +                                                                                              
      286 +L4 — Deferring stop updates to the next bar (pending_stop pattern).                           
      287 +     Fix: apply MFE lock immediately and check same-bar exit.                                 
      288 +                                                                                              
      289 +L5 — Checking TP before SL on the same bar.                                                   
      290 +     Fix: always check SL first (Rule 9). For longs: low before high.                         
      291 +                                                                                              
      292 +L6 — Exiting at bar.low (long) or bar.high (short) instead of stop price.                     
      293 +     Fix: compute R from stop_price, not from bar extreme.                                    
      294 +                                                                                              
      295 +L7 — Loading 4h candles independently from the DB instead of resampling 5m.                   
      296 +     Fix: always build_4h_rsi(df5m) — never query 4h directly.                                
      297 +                                                                                              
      298 +L8 — Using ATR or any indicator from the entry bar to set stop or size.                       
      299 +     Fix: all indicator values used at entry must be from bars[0..i-1].                       
      300 +                                                                                              
      301 +L9 — Not excluding trades whose exit falls outside the backtest window.                       
      302 +     Fix: filter trades by exit timestamp, not entry timestamp.                               
      303 +                                                                                              
      304 +L10 — Pyramiding: entering a second position while the first is open.                         
      305 +      Fix: skip signals when position > 0 on that symbol.                                     
      306  """
      307

⏺ Now I have a thorough picture of what exists. Here's my analysis and a proposed design:

  ---
  What Already Exists

  The project already has solid pieces:
  - simulation/ — entry/exit logic (4h RSI entries, 5m MFE-ladder replay)
  - study/ — exploratory market research scripts
  - scripts/ — CLI runners that orchestrate full backtests
  - runs/ — timestamped run artifacts (webapp auto-discovers these)
  - webapp/ — React dashboard that reads runs + candle DB

  The gap is: no standard contract for what a "strategy" or "study" looks like, so each new script is one-off
  and the webapp can't generically consume new work.

  ---
  Proposed Design: playground/ folder

  Rather than modifying the existing simulation code (which works), create a new playground/ folder that wraps
  it with standards. Existing scripts keep running as-is.

  playground/
  ├── base/
  │   ├── strategy.py        # Abstract base class for any strategy
  │   ├── study.py           # Abstract base class for any study
  │   ├── schemas.py         # Standard dataclasses (Trade, StudyResult, RunManifest)
  │   └── sim_rules.py       # Documented simulation assumptions/rules
  ├── engine/
  │   ├── candle_sim.py      # Standard sim engine (enforces rules)
  │   └── run_writer.py      # Writes outputs in webapp-compatible run format
  ├── strategies/            # Agent-created strategies go here
  │   └── _example/          # Reference implementation
  └── studies/               # Agent-created studies go here
      └── _example/          # Reference implementation

  ---
  The Three Standards

  1. Simulation Rules (sim_rules.py)

  Codified assumptions so any agent knows what is and isn't valid:
  - Entries only on bar close (no look-ahead)
  - Fills at open of next bar (configurable slippage offset)
  - Round-trip fee in bps (must be declared)
  - No partial fills — full fill assumed
  - SL/TP checked against candle high/low (not tick data — worst-case resolution)
  - One position per asset at a time

  2. Study Standard (BaseStudy)

  Every study must produce:
  study_output/
    manifest.json     # name, version, assets, timeframe, date range, run_ts
    summary.json      # key metrics dict
    events.csv        # raw event rows (standardized columns)
    README.md         # auto-generated from docstring + summary

  3. Strategy/Simulation Standard (BaseStrategy + RunWriter)

  Every simulation writes to runs/ in the existing format the webapp already reads, plus a manifest.json the
  webapp can use to label/filter runs:
  runs/run_<name>_<ts>/
    manifest.json     # strategy name, params, assumptions declared
    artifacts/
      summary.csv     # per-chunk metrics (same schema as existing)
      metrics.json    # aggregate stats
    trades/
      <ASSET>.csv     # per-asset trade ledger (same schema as existing)

  ---
  Options to Proceed

  A. Create playground/ now — build the base classes, schemas, sim rules, and one reference strategy that wraps
  the existing RSI sim. Clean separation, existing code untouched.

  B. Audit first — I read the existing simulation/ and study/ files in detail, then we decide exactly what to
  copy vs. refactor before writing anything.

  C. Minimal MVP — just schemas.py + sim_rules.py as a written contract (no classes yet), plus a run_writer.py
  that any script can call to emit webapp-compatible output.

  Which direction fits best, and do the simulation rules I listed match your assumptions? Any I'm missing (e.g.,
   how you handle the case where SL and TP are both hit in the same bar)?

  ---
  Audit Findings

  What's solid and shouldn't be touched

  - simulation/ltf_trade_management_study.py — the ReplayResult dataclass and replay_trade_mfe_ladder_5m() are
  mature, well-commented, with documented assumptions. This is the best-written code in the project.
  - run_config.json → runs/ folder structure already works as a contract the webapp reads.
  - The trade CSV schema (from the actual files) is already a de facto standard — the webapp's parseTradeCsv()
  explicitly knows which fields are numeric.

  Problems found (duplications & inconsistencies)

  1. load_merged_5m is defined in scripts/massive_chunk_backtest_5m.py and duplicated in
  massive_chunk_backtest_5m_v1fix.py. Every study file imports it from a script:
  from massive_chunk_backtest_5m_v1fix import load_merged_5m  # in study/*.py
  Studies importing from scripts is backwards — utilities should flow the other way.

  2. wilder_atr() is copy-pasted verbatim in both study/atr_random_entry_study.py and
  study/xrp_fvg_regime_concepts_study.py.

  3. _fee_r() and ReplayResult are duplicated between ltf_trade_management_study.py and
  ltf_trade_management_study_v1fix.py (v1fix appears to be a near-copy of the original).

  4. No study has standardized output. Some print to stdout, some write CSVs to study/out/, some write nowhere.
  There's no manifest.json or summary schema.

  5. Webapp has a hardcoded trade file regex:
  /^trade_details_(v1fix|v1)_(tp[0-9p]+)\.csv$/i
  Any new strategy that doesn't name its files trade_details_v1_tp*.csv will be invisible to the webapp.

  6. run_config.json schema is implicit — no validation, no documented required fields. The webapp silently
  fails if it's missing.

  ---
  Recommendation

  Given all this, here's what makes sense:

  Step 2 — Create playground/

  playground/
  ├── __init__.py
  ├── sim_rules.py        # Written record of all assumptions above
  ├── schemas.py          # Dataclasses: TradeRecord, StudyManifest, RunManifest
  ├── base_study.py       # Abstract: run() → StudyResult, auto-writes manifest.json + events.csv
  ├── base_strategy.py    # Abstract: generate_signals() + replay() → writes run folder
  └── run_writer.py       # Handles the runs/ folder structure + run_config.json format

  Step 3 — Update the webapp's file regex

  Generalize index.cjs:116 from hardcoded v1fix|v1 to accept any trade_details_<name>_tp*.csv pattern, so new
  strategies automatically appear.

  What NOT to touch

⏺ Good question — the existing webapp has real value (candlestick charts + trade overlays work well) but the
  React+Node stack is a burden to maintain and agents can't contribute to it. Here's the honest comparison:

  ---
  Option A: Keep the webapp

  Pros: TradingView-quality charts already work, 4h+5m overlay is built
  Cons: React+Node — agents can't write visualization code, hardcoded file patterns, requires running two
  servers, hard to extend

  Option B: Replace with Streamlit

  Pros:
  - Pure Python — agents write strategy code AND visualization code in the same language
  - Reads your standardized CSVs/JSONs directly, no backend server
  - streamlit-lightweight-charts gives the same TradingView-quality candlesticks
  - One command: streamlit run lab/app.py
  - Each strategy/study can ship its own Streamlit page
  - Hot reload, easy to audit

  Cons: Slightly less polished than a custom React app, some layout constraints

  Option C: Marimo notebooks

  Reactive Python notebooks that can run as webapps. Good but less ecosystem maturity than Streamlit.

  ---
  My recommendation: Streamlit

  It's the right fit because the whole point is agents producing auditable outputs. If an agent writes a
  strategy, it also writes:
  1. The strategy logic (strategies/rsi_4h/strategy.py)
  2. The simulation output (runs/ CSVs)
  3. A Streamlit page that visualizes it (strategies/rsi_4h/viz.py)

  The main lab/app.py is a dashboard that auto-discovers all runs and lets you drill into any of them — same
  concept as the existing webapp, but everything in Python.

  ---
  Shall I:
  1. Create the lab/ folder with the full structure
  2. Port the RSI 4h strategy in as the reference implementation
  3. Build a Streamlit app that replicates what the existing webapp does (trade list + 4h chart + 5m detail +
  equity curve)

  And we leave the existing webapp as-is (don't delete it, just stop developing it)?

⏺ Found both flaws. The differences are clear and specific. Let me document them before touching code.

  ---
  The two flaws in the original code (vs v1fix)

  Flaw 1 — The big one: entry bar grace period

  Original replay_trade_mfe_ladder_5m:
  skip_entry_bucket_hours: float = 4.0   # ← FLAW
  V1fix:
  skip_entry_bucket_hours: float = 0.0   # ← FIX

  With skip=4.0, SL and TP cannot fire during the 4h entry candle. The trade gets a 4h immunity window after
  entry. In reality, your stop is live from the moment you enter. Many trades that would have immediately
  reversed and stopped out in the entry bar were artificially kept alive — this is why results looked too good.

  Flaw 2 — Deferred stop updates

  Original uses pending_stop — when MFE triggers the lock level, the stop only moves at the next bar's open:
  pending_stop = desired   # queued, not active yet
  V1fix applies the lock immediately in the same bar — the tighter stop can be hit by the same candle's adverse
  wick. More realistic: in real trading, your stop-limit can be triggered the moment price reverses after
  hitting the MFE level.

  Now fixing both in the lab:

⏺ Good. Here's a summary of what was found and fixed:

  ---
  The two flaws, explained plainly

  Flaw 1 — Entry bar grace period (skip=4.0)

  The original code said "don't check for stops or exits for the first 4 hours after entry." In reality, the
  moment you buy, your stop is placed. If price immediately reverses and hits your stop in the same 4h candle,
  you're out. The original was preventing this, making trades survive adverse moves they wouldn't survive in
  practice. This is the primary reason results looked too good.

  Flaw 2 — Deferred stop updates

  When MFE triggered a tighter stop, the original queued it for the next bar. So if a 5m bar reached +1R and
  immediately reversed to +0.8R (whipsaw), the trade continued unaffected because the lock wasn't live yet.
  V1fix activates the lock in the same bar — if price touches +1R and reverses to +0.8R in the same candle, you
  exit at +0.8R.

  Both are now fixed in lab/sim/exit.py and documented in lab/sim/rules.py (Rules 6 and 7) with the "why it
  matters" explanation so any agent reading the rules understands the reasoning, not just the rule.
