      135 +If you want to model gap fills, add a gap_slippage parameter explicitly.                      
      136 +                                                                                              
      137 +═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════                   
      138 +SECTION F — TAKE PROFIT: PLACEMENT AND FILL                                                   
      139 +═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════                   
      140 +                                                                                              
      141 +RULE 8 — TP is hit when the bar's High (long) or Low (short) reaches the TP                   
      142 +price. Fill at TP price, not beyond it.                                                       
      143 +                                                                                              
      144 +  Long TP hit:  bar.high >= tp_price → exit at tp_price                                       
      145 +  Short TP hit: bar.low  <= tp_price → exit at tp_price                                       
      146 +                                                                                              
      147 +Do not fill at bar.high — that would assume you got filled at the extreme,                    
      148 +which overstates profits.                                                                     
      149 +                                                                                              
      150 +═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════                   
      151 +SECTION G — SAME-BAR AMBIGUITY: SL AND TP BOTH HIT                                            
      152 +═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════                   
      153 +                                                                                              
      154 +RULE 9 — When both SL and TP are reachable within the same bar, SL wins.                      
      155 +                                                                                              
      156 +  Long:  bar.low <= SL and bar.high >= TP → exit at SL (conservative)                         
      157 +  Short: bar.high >= SL and bar.low <= TP → exit at SL (conservative)                         
      158 +                                                                                              
      159 +This is the conservative assumption: when we don't know the intrabar order,                   
      160 +we assume the adverse move came first. This slightly penalizes the strategy                   
      161 +vs optimistic assumptions, which is the correct direction for avoiding                        
      162 +overfitted results.                                                                           
      163 +                                                                                              
      164 +Bar-level exit check order (within each 5m bar):                                              
      165 +  1. Check SL                                                                                 
      166 +  2. If not stopped: check TP                                                                 
      167 +  3. If not exited: check MFE ladder triggers, update stop                                    
      168 +  4. If stop moved: check if new stop is immediately hit (same-bar activation)                
      169 +                                                                                              
      170 +For longs: check low before high.                                                             
      171 +For shorts: check high before low.                                                            
      172 +                                                                                              
      173 +═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════                   
      174 +SECTION H — TRADE MANAGEMENT: MFE LADDER AND STOP UPDATES                                     
      175 +═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════                   
      176 +                                                                                              
      177 +RULE 10 — MFE (Maximum Favorable Excursion) is tracked cumulatively from                      
      178 +entry. MFE is expressed in R-units: mfe_r = (peak_price - entry) / risk.                      
      179 +                                                                                              
      180 +RULE 11 — When an MFE threshold triggers a stop update, the new stop is                       
      181 +active IMMEDIATELY in the same bar (same-bar activation).                                     
      182 +                                                                                              
      183 +  CORRECT (same-bar):                                                                         
      184 +    bar.high >= entry + mfe_r * risk                                                          
      185 +    → update stop to entry + lock_r * risk                                                    
      186 +    → check if bar.low <= new stop in the SAME bar                                            
      187 +    → if yes: exit at new stop price                                                          
      188 +                                                                                              
      189 +  WRONG (deferred, the original bug):                                                         
      190 +    bar.high >= mfe_r threshold                                                               
      191 +    → queue new stop for NEXT bar                                                             
      192 +    → bar can whipsaw without hitting new stop                                                
      193 +                                                                                              
      194 +WHY: In the original code, a whipsaw bar (price moves to +1R then drops to                    
      195 ++0.8R in the same 5m candle) would NOT trigger the lock — the stop only moved                 
      196 +at the next bar. This gave trades a free pass through whipsaw bars, inflating                 
      197 +managed R. Same-bar activation is more realistic: the lock fires when price                   
      198 +trades there, regardless of when in the bar it happened.                                      
      199 +                                                                                              
      200 +RULE 12 — MFE cap: lock level cannot exceed MFE actually reached.                             
      201 +                                                                                              
      202 +  lock_eff = min(lock_r, mfe_max_r)   ← cap_lock_by_mfe = True (default)                      
      203 +                                                                                              
      204 +You cannot lock in +0.8R if price has only moved +0.5R. The stop update                       
      205 +is: max(current_stop, entry + min(lock_r, mfe_max_r) * risk) for longs.                       
      206 +                                                                                              
      207 +WHY: Without this cap, a stage defined as (mfe=1.0R, lock=0.8R) would move                    
      208 +your stop to +0.8R even if the MFE was only 1.0R by 1 tick. With the cap,                     
      209 +lock_eff = min(0.8, 1.0) = 0.8R. In practice this rarely differs, but at                      
      210 +exactly the threshold it prevents an unrealistic exact-tick lock.                             
      211 +                                                                                              
      212 +═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════                   
      213 +SECTION I — FEE MODEL                                                                         
      214 +═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════                   
      215 +                                                                                              
      216 +RULE 13 — Fee is round-trip (entry + exit combined), expressed in R-units.                    
      217 +                                                                                              
      218 +  fee_r = entry_price * fee_bps / 10_000 / risk                                               
      219 +                                                                                              
      220 +This fee is subtracted from the gross R at the end of the trade.                              
      221 +Default: 3.0 bps RT. This is approximate for liquid crypto spot/perp markets.                 
      222 +                                                                                              
      223 +Deduct fee once per trade regardless of how many stop updates happened.                       
      224 +Fee does not change when the stop moves (we are not modeling re-hedging costs).               
      225 +                                                                                              
      226 +═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════                   
      227 +SECTION J — DATA SOURCE AND QUALITY                                                           
      228 +═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════                   
      229 +                                                                                              
      230 +RULE 14 — All 5m candles come from the shared SQLite DB via core/db.py.                       
      231 +Use load_merged_5m(db_path, symbol) — never query the DB directly in                          
      232 +strategy code. This ensures consistent deduplication across sessions.                         
      233 +                                                                                              
      234 +RULE 15 — Data coverage must be validated before a simulation run.                            
      235 +                                                                                              
      236 +Before running a strategy, check:                                                             
      237 +  - Symbol has data from at least start_utc                                                   
      238 +  - No large gaps (>= 2h of missing 5m bars) in the backtest window                           
      239 +  - Minimum bar count: at least sl_n + rsi_window + 10 bars in the HTF series                 
      240 +                                                                                              
      241 +Trades that start outside the validated data window must be excluded.                         
      242 +                                                                                              
      243 +RULE 16 — The backtest window is [start_utc, end_utc). Half-open interval.                    
      244 +Trades are assigned to time chunks by their EXIT timestamp, not entry.                        
      245 +                                                                                              
      246 +═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════                   
      247 +SECTION K — KNOWN OPTIMISMS (ACCEPTABLE TRADE-OFFS)                                           
      248 +═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════                   
      249 +                                                                                              
      250 +The following are known ways the simulation is still more favorable than                      
      251 +live trading. They are accepted trade-offs, not bugs. Document any that                       
      252 +significantly affect your strategy's edge.                                                    
      253 +                                                                                              
      254 +K1 — Zero slippage: fills assumed at exact open/SL/TP prices.                                 
      255 +     Real fills may be worse, especially in fast markets.                                     
      256 +                                                                                              
      257 +K2 — Infinite liquidity: full fill assumed at all levels.                                     
      258 +     Real fills may be partial for large sizes or at illiquid levels.                         
      259 +                                                                                              
      260 +K3 — Bid/ask spread not modeled: fee_bps approximates this but                                
      261 +     spread can be higher in volatile periods.                                                
      262 +                                                                                              
      263 +K4 — Bar high/low order unknown: we assume conservative order (adverse first)                 
      264 +     but sometimes the favorable move does come first in reality.                             
      265 +                                                                                              
      266 +K5 — No funding rate (for perpetual futures strategies): if modeling perps,                   
      267 +     funding must be added as a periodic cost.                                                
      268 +                                                                                              
      269 +K6 — 5m bar resolution: intrabar path is unknown. Events that happen                          
      270 +     between 5m bar opens cannot be modeled. Tight stops near the entry                       
      271 +     price may produce different results in reality than in simulation.                       
      272 +                                                                                              
      273 +═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════                   
      274 +SECTION L — COMMON BUGS TO AVOID                                                              
      275 +═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════                   
      276 +                                                                                              
      277 +L1 — Using bar i's close to both generate a signal AND enter at bar i.                        
      278 +     Fix: signal at close[i-1] → entry at open[i].                                            
      279 +                                                                                              
      280 +L2 — Using bar i's high/low in the structural stop when entering at open[i].                  
      281 +     Fix: stop = min(low[i-sl_n : i]) — slice ends before i (not i+1).                        
      282 +                                                                                              
      283 +L3 — Starting the 5m replay after the 4h entry candle (skip=4h).                              
      284 +     Fix: skip_entry_bucket_hours=0.0. Stop is live from entry.                               
      285 +                                                                                              
      286 +L4 — Deferring stop updates to the next bar (pending_stop pattern).                           
      287 +     Fix: apply MFE lock immediately and check same-bar exit.                                 
      288 +                                                                                              
      289 +L5 — Checking TP before SL on the same bar.                                                   
      290 +     Fix: always check SL first (Rule 9). For longs: low before high.                         
      291 +                                                                                              
      292 +L6 — Exiting at bar.low (long) or bar.high (short) instead of stop price.                     
      293 +     Fix: compute R from stop_price, not from bar extreme.                                    
      294 +                                                                                              
      295 +L7 — Loading 4h candles independently from the DB instead of resampling 5m.                   
      296 +     Fix: always build_4h_rsi(df5m) — never query 4h directly.                                
      297 +                                                                                              
      298 +L8 — Using ATR or any indicator from the entry bar to set stop or size.                       
      299 +     Fix: all indicator values used at entry must be from bars[0..i-1].                       
      300 +                                                                                              
      301 +L9 — Not excluding trades whose exit falls outside the backtest window.                       
      302 +     Fix: filter trades by exit timestamp, not entry timestamp.                               
      303 +                                                                                              
      304 +L10 — Pyramiding: entering a second position while the first is open.                         
      305 +      Fix: skip signals when position > 0 on that symbol.                                     
      306  """
      307

      320 +    """                                                                                       
      321 +    Add vertical rectangle shading behind the 4h chart based on structure.                    
      322 +    BALANCED = subtle green, IMBALANCED = subtle red.

      329 +    timestamps     = regime_slice.index

      334 +        if pd.isna(s):

      336 +            continue                                                                          
      337 +        j = i + 1

      348 +        )

⏺ Done. Here's what was updated in lab/app.py:

  New loader (load_regime_df): reads artifacts/regime_{symbol}.csv from the run folder, parses the UTC index.
  Returns empty DataFrame if the file doesn't exist (backward compatible with RSI4h runs).

  trade_chart_fig now accepts an optional regime_df parameter. When present:
  - Expands to 4 rows (was 3): OHLCV + BB Bands / RSI / Regime / 5m Detail
  - Row 1: BB band lines (upper, mid, lower) drawn as dotted blue/grey overlays, plus BALANCED (green) /
  IMBALANCED (red) background shading via add_vrect
  - Row 3 (new): Step-function traces for structure_num (0=BALANCED, 1=IMBALANCED, filled green) and vol_num
  (0=LOW, 1=NORMAL, 2=HIGH, orange line)
  - When no regime data exists (RSI4h runs), the chart renders exactly as before — 3 rows, no BB bands, no
  shading

  Chart tab: loads regime CSV alongside candles, passes it to trade_chart_fig, shows a caption explaining the
  regime panel axis values.

      318  
      319 +def _add_regime_shading(fig: go.Figure, regime_slice: pd.DataFrame) -> None:                  
      320 +    """                                                                                       
      321 +    Add vertical rectangle shading behind the 4h chart based on structure.                    
      322 +    BALANCED = subtle green, IMBALANCED = subtle red.                                         
      323 +    Only draws transitions (groups contiguous same-structure bars into one vrect).            
      324 +    """                                                                                       
      325 +    if "structure" not in regime_slice.columns or len(regime_slice) == 0:                     
      326 +        return                                                                                
      327 +                                                                                              
      328 +    structure_vals = regime_slice["structure"].values                                         
      329 +    timestamps     = regime_slice.index                                                       
      330 +                                                                                              
      331 +    i = 0                                                                                     
      332 +    while i < len(structure_vals):                                                            
      333 +        s = structure_vals[i]                                                                 
      334 +        if pd.isna(s):                                                                        
      335 +            i += 1                                                                            
      336 +            continue                                                                          
      337 +        j = i + 1                                                                             
      338 +        while j < len(structure_vals) and structure_vals[j] == s:                             
      339 +            j += 1

  New loader (load_regime_df): reads artifacts/regime_{symbol}.csv from the run folder, parses the UTC index.
  Returns empty DataFrame if the file doesn't exist (backward compatible with RSI4h runs).

  - Expands to 4 rows (was 3): OHLCV + BB Bands / RSI / Regime / 5m Detail
  - Row 1: BB band lines (upper, mid, lower) drawn as dotted blue/grey overlays, plus BALANCED (green) /
  IMBALANCED (red) background shading via add_vrect
  - Row 3 (new): Step-function traces for structure_num (0=BALANCED, 1=IMBALANCED, filled green) and vol_num
  (0=LOW, 1=NORMAL, 2=HIGH, orange line)
  - When no regime data exists (RSI4h runs), the chart renders exactly as before — 3 rows, no BB bands, no
  shading

  Chart tab: loads regime CSV alongside candles, passes it to trade_chart_fig, shows a caption explaining the
  regime panel axis values.

 Bash command                                                                                                   
                                                                                                              
   source .venv/bin/activate && python3 - << 'EOF'                                                              
   import pandas as pd
   import numpy as np

   df = pd.read_csv("runs/run_bb_balanced_20260413_040913/trades/trade_details_bb_balanced_tp2p0.csv")

   # BB width band: entry price to midband = half-band distance
   # For a long: entry is below lower band, TP at midband would be (mid - entry)
   # bb_width is percentage width of full band: (upper - lower) / mid * 100
   # So half-band from lower to mid = bb_width/2 pct of mid price

   # Compute theoretical TP at midband as R multiple
   if all(c in df.columns for c in ['entry_price','bb_mid','bb_lower','bb_upper','risk','side']):
       # Distance from entry to midband
       df['mid_dist'] = np.where(df['side']==1, df['bb_mid'] - df['entry_price'], df['entry_price'] -
   df['bb_mid'])
       df['mid_r'] = df['mid_dist'] / df['risk']
       print("=== R-multiple needed to reach BB midband (TP at mid) ===")
       print(f"  Mean:   {df['mid_r'].mean():.2f}R")
       print(f"  Median: {df['mid_r'].median():.2f}R")

⏺ Done. Here's what was updated in lab/app.py:

  New loader (load_regime_df): reads artifacts/regime_{symbol}.csv from the run folder, parses the UTC index.
  Returns empty DataFrame if the file doesn't exist (backward compatible with RSI4h runs).

  trade_chart_fig now accepts an optional regime_df parameter. When present:
  - Expands to 4 rows (was 3): OHLCV + BB Bands / RSI / Regime / 5m Detail
  - Row 1: BB band lines (upper, mid, lower) drawn as dotted blue/grey overlays, plus BALANCED (green) /
  IMBALANCED (red) background shading via add_vrect
  - Row 3 (new): Step-function traces for structure_num (0=BALANCED, 1=IMBALANCED, filled green) and vol_num
  (0=LOW, 1=NORMAL, 2=HIGH, orange line)
  - When no regime data exists (RSI4h runs), the chart renders exactly as before — 3 rows, no BB bands, no
  shading

  Chart tab: loads regime CSV alongside candles, passes it to trade_chart_fig, shows a caption explaining the
  regime panel axis values.

 Bash command                                                                                                   
                                                                                                                
   source .venv/bin/activate && python3 - << 'EOF'
   import pandas as pd
   import numpy as np

   df = pd.read_csv("runs/run_bb_balanced_20260413_040913/trades/trade_details_bb_balanced_tp2p0.csv")

   # The key question: if TP were AT the midband price (not a fixed R), how would R look?
   # mid_r = distance to midband / risk (computed earlier)
   # If price reaches mid, we exit at mid_r * risk P&L
   # A trade hits mid if: for longs, high >= bb_mid; for shorts, low <= bb_mid
   # We don't have MFE data, but we can check: trades that hit TP (2.0R) certainly passed through mid (1.07R
   avg)
   # Trades that hit SL: did they ever reach mid? We don't know exact MFE.

   # But we can simulate: if TP = midband, and SL = ATR*1.5
   # The win/loss outcome doesn't change (same SL), but the P&L on wins changes to mid_r instead of 2R

   df['mid_dist'] = np.where(df['side']==1, df['bb_mid'] - df['entry_price'], df['entry_price'] -
   df['bb_mid'])
   df['mid_r'] = df['mid_dist'] / df['risk']

   # For TP-hit trades: their actual P&L would be mid_r (not tp_r=2.0)
   # For SL-hit trades: unchanged (we don't know if mid was reached)
   df['simulated_mid_r'] = np.where(
       df['managed_reason'] == 'TP',
       df['mid_r'],  # exit at mid
       df['managed_r']  # SL hit unchanged (worst case: assume no mid reached)
   )

   print("=== Simulated: TP at midband price (same SL) ===")
   print(f"  Total R: {df['simulated_mid_r'].sum():.2f}  (vs {df['managed_r'].sum():.2f} at 2.0R fixed)")
   print(f"  Win %:   {(df['simulated_mid_r']>0).mean()*100:.1f}%")
   print(f"  Avg R:   {df['simulated_mid_r'].mean():.4f}")

   for vol, g in df.groupby('vol'):
       sim = np.where(g['managed_reason']=='TP', g['mid_r'], g['managed_r'])
       print(f"  {vol:8s}: total={sim.sum():.2f}R  win={(sim>0).mean()*100:.1f}%")

   print("\n=== Simulated: TP at mid, shorts only ===")
   sh = df[df['side']==-1]
   sim_sh = np.where(sh['managed_reason']=='TP', sh['mid_r'], sh['managed_r'])
   print(f"  Total R: {sim_sh.sum():.2f}  n={len(sh)}")

   print("\n=== Simulated: TP at mid, longs only ===")
   lo = df[df['side']==1]
   sim_lo = np.where(lo['managed_reason']=='TP', lo['mid_r'], lo['managed_r'])
   print(f"  Total R: {sim_lo.sum():.2f}  n={len(lo)}")

   # How tight does the stop need to be to make midband = 1.5R?
   print("\n=== Required ATR mult for midband to equal target R ===")
   # mid_r = half_band / (atr * mult)
   # If we want mid_r = 1.5: mult = half_band / (atr * 1.5) → already computed
   df['half_band_price'] = (df['bb_upper'] - df['bb_lower']) / 2
   df['atr_for_mid_1p5'] = df['half_band_price'] / (1.5 * df['atr'])  # this is the atr_mult needed
   df['atr_for_mid_2p0'] = df['half_band_price'] / (2.0 * df['atr'])
   print(f"  ATR mult needed for midband = 1.5R: mean={df['atr_for_mid_1p5'].mean():.2f}
   median={df['atr_for_mid_1p5'].median():.2f}")
   print(f"  ATR mult needed for midband = 2.0R: mean={df['atr_for_mid_2p0'].mean():.2f}
   median={df['atr_for_mid_2p0'].median():.2f}")
   EOF

      348 +        )

⏺ Done. Here's what was updated in lab/app.py:

  New loader (load_regime_df): reads artifacts/regime_{symbol}.csv from the run folder, parses the UTC index.
  Returns empty DataFrame if the file doesn't exist (backward compatible with RSI4h runs).

  trade_chart_fig now accepts an optional regime_df parameter. When present:
  - Expands to 4 rows (was 3): OHLCV + BB Bands / RSI / Regime / 5m Detail
  - Row 1: BB band lines (upper, mid, lower) drawn as dotted blue/grey overlays, plus BALANCED (green) /
  IMBALANCED (red) background shading via add_vrect
  - Row 3 (new): Step-function traces for structure_num (0=BALANCED, 1=IMBALANCED, filled green) and vol_num
  (0=LOW, 1=NORMAL, 2=HIGH, orange line)
  - When no regime data exists (RSI4h runs), the chart renders exactly as before — 3 rows, no BB bands, no
  shading

  Chart tab: loads regime CSV alongside candles, passes it to trade_chart_fig, shows a caption explaining the
  regime panel axis values.

      import pandas as pd
      import numpy as np

      df = pd.read_csv("runs/run_bb_balanced_20260413_040913/trades/trade_details_bb_balanced_tp2p0.csv")

      # The key question: if TP were AT the midband price (not a fixed R), how would R look?
      # mid_r = distance to midband / risk (computed earlier)
      # If price reaches mid, we exit at mid_r * risk P&L
      # A trade hits mid if: for longs, high >= bb_mid; for shorts, low <= bb_mid
      # We don't have MFE data, but we can check: trades that hit TP (2.0R) certainly passed through mid (1.07R
      avg)
      # Trades that hit SL: did they ever reach mid? We don't know exact MFE.

      # But we can simulate: if TP = midband, and SL = ATR*1.5
      # The win/loss outcome doesn't change (same SL), but the P&L on wins changes to mid_r instead of 2R

      df['mid_dist'] = np.where(df['side']==1, df['bb_mid'] - df['entry_price'], df['entry_price'] -
      df['bb_mid'])
      df['mid_r'] = df['mid_dist'] / df['risk']

      # For TP-hit trades: their actual P&L would be mid_r (not tp_r=2.0)
      # For SL-hit trades: unchanged (we don't know if mid was reached)
      df['simulated_mid_r'] = np.where(
          df['managed_reason'] == 'TP',
          df['mid_r'],  # exit at mid
          df['managed_r']  # SL hit unchanged (worst case: assume no mid reached)
      )

      print("=== Simulated: TP at midband price (same SL) ===")
      print(f"  Total R: {df['simulated_mid_r'].sum():.2f}  (vs {df['managed_r'].sum():.2f} at 2.0R fixed)")

          sim = np.where(g['managed_reason']=='TP', g['mid_r'], g['managed_r'])
          print(f"  {vol:8s}: total={sim.sum():.2f}R  win={(sim>0).mean()*100:.1f}%")

      print("\n=== Simulated: TP at mid, shorts only ===")

      print(f"  ATR mult needed for midband = 1.5R: mean={df['atr_for_mid_1p5'].mean():.2f}

  Key findings from the data:                                                                                   
  - HIGH vol is the only regime with positive R, but only n=28 (too small to trust alone)                       
  - Short/Long asymmetry is massive: shorts are breakeven-to-positive across all TPs, longs are deeply negative 
  — the ATR stop is 1.23× wider than the half-band, meaning you're risking more than the natural reversal target
   distance                                                                                                     
  - TP at midband makes it worse at current stop sizing because midband is only ~1.07R away — that's below the
  fee threshold to be useful                                                                                    
  - To make midband = 1.5R, you need ATR mult ~0.88; for 2.0R you need ~0.66 — the stop needs to come in        
  significantly                                                                                         
  - Two sweeps worth running: (1) ATR mult tightness with TP at midband, (2) Shorts-only with same

⏺ Results are in. Let me compile the full picture:                                                              
                                                                                                                
  ---                                                                                                           
  Vol regime answer:                                                                                            
  - In the fixed-R baseline (original run): HIGH vol slightly better (+5.62R at 1R TP, n=28)                    
  - In the TP-at-midband shorts sweep: LOW vol dramatically better (72.2% win, +5.20R, n=18)                    
  - Neither is reliable — both have n<30, which is statistically noise                                          
                                                                                                                
  The sweeps reveal the real problem:                                                                           
                                                                                                                
  Sweep A — ATR mult × TP at midband:                                                                           
  The wider the stop, the better — which is the opposite of your hypothesis. Tighter stops destroy R/R because  
  the midband is ~1R away regardless of stop width (it's a moving target, not a fixed level). At ATR×0.4 you    
  need 18% wins just to break even on midband trades. You never get there. The midband-as-TP idea doesn't work
  because the midband drifts with price during the hold period — it's not a static target.                      
                                                            
  Sweep B — Shorts only, TP at midband:                                                                         
  Shorts are consistently better than the full pool, but still all negative. At ATR×1.5 shorts are at -39R vs
  -244R for all trades — cleaner but not profitable.                                                            
                                                            
  Sweep C — Vol breakdown at ATR×1.5, shorts, TP at midband:                                                    
                                                            
  ┌────────┬──────┬─────────┬───────┐                                                                           
  │  Vol   │  n   │ total R │ win%  │                       
  ├────────┼──────┼─────────┼───────┤
  │ LOW    │ 18   │ +5.20   │ 72.2% │
  ├────────┼──────┼─────────┼───────┤
  │ HIGH   │ 27   │ -0.74   │ 40.7% │                                                                           
  ├────────┼──────┼─────────┼───────┤
  │ NORMAL │ 1122 │ -43.88  │ 46.8% │                                                                           
  └────────┴──────┴─────────┴───────┘                       

  The actual diagnosis:                                                                                         
  
  The strategy has a structural problem, not a parameter problem. On 1h XRP 2022–2026:                          
  - 1,122 out of 1,190 trades are NORMAL vol — that pool is reliably negative and drowns everything else
  - The long side is broken at every configuration (XRP had extended downtrends in 2022-2023 — BB longs below   
  lower band are fading a trend, not reverting)                                                              
  - The BB period (20) on 1h bars produces ~2523 BALANCED signals — too many, too noisy                         
                                                                                       
  The one thread worth pursuing: LOW vol BALANCED shorts with TP at midband. 72% win rate needs to be validated 
  on more symbols and a wider date range before it means anything. The current n=18 could flip on a single bad  
  month.                                                                                                        
                                                                                                                
  Next 3 experiments to run:                                                                                    
  1. Multi-symbol LOW vol BALANCED shorts — run the same config on BTC, ETH, SOL, LINK from 2022 and check if
  the 72% win rate holds or is XRP-specific                                                                     
  2. BB period sweep on 1h — test bb_period=[30, 50, 100] to reduce NORMAL-vol noise; longer bands produce fewer
   but higher-conviction signals                                                                                
  3. IMBALANCED regime shorts — your trend-following intuition is probably right; BB upper band in IMBALANCED   
  structure may work better as a momentum continuation entry than a mean-reversion short

   import pandas as pd
   import numpy as np
   import sys
   sys.path.insert(0, '.')
   from lab.core.db import load_merged_5m
   from lab.core.resample import resample_ohlcv
   from lab.core.regime import classify_regimes

   df5 = load_merged_5m("/Users/anibalperez/revolutions/backtester/data/backtest.sqlite", "XRPUSDT")
   df5 = df5.loc[df5.index >= pd.Timestamp("2022-01-01", tz="UTC")]
   df1h = resample_ohlcv(df5, "1h").copy()
   df1h = classify_regimes(df1h, atr_period=14, atr_ma_period=50, er_period=20, er_balanced_threshold=0.35)

   r = df1h["atr_ratio"].dropna()
   print("ATR ratio distribution:")
   print(f"  p10={r.quantile(0.10):.3f}  p25={r.quantile(0.25):.3f}  p33={r.quantile(0.33):.3f}")
   print(f"  p50={r.quantile(0.50):.3f}  p67={r.quantile(0.67):.3f}  p75={r.quantile(0.75):.3f}")
   print(f"  p90={r.quantile(0.90):.3f}  p95={r.quantile(0.95):.3f}  p99={r.quantile(0.99):.3f}")
   print(f"  mean={r.mean():.3f}  std={r.std():.3f}  max={r.max():.3f}")
   print(f"\nCurrent thresholds LOW<0.6, HIGH>1.5:")
   print(f"  LOW:    {(r<0.6).sum():4d} bars  {(r<0.6).mean()*100:.1f}%")
   print(f"  NORMAL: {((r>=0.6)&(r<=1.5)).sum():4d} bars  {((r>=0.6)&(r<=1.5)).mean()*100:.1f}%")
   print(f"  HIGH:   {(r>1.5).sum():4d} bars  {(r>1.5).mean()*100:.1f}%")
   print(f"\nQuantile-based thirds (p33/p67):")
   p33, p67 = r.quantile(0.33), r.quantile(0.67)
   print(f"  LOW  (<{p33:.3f}): {(r<p33).sum():4d} bars  {(r<p33).mean()*100:.1f}%")
   print(f"  MED  ({p33:.3f}-{p67:.3f}): {((r>=p33)&(r<p67)).sum():4d} bars
   {((r>=p33)&(r<p67)).mean()*100:.1f}%")
   print(f"  HIGH (>{p67:.3f}): {(r>=p67).sum():4d} bars  {(r>=p67).mean()*100:.1f}%")
   print(f"\nStructure split:")
   print(df1h['structure'].value_counts())
   print(f"\nTotal 1h bars: {len(df1h)}, with regime: {df1h['structure'].notna().sum()}")

   # Also look at what candle data looks like for price action
   df1h['close_pct'] = (df1h['close'] - df1h['low']) / (df1h['high'] - df1h['low'])
   df1h['body_pct']  = abs(df1h['close'] - df1h['open']) / (df1h['high'] - df1h['low'])
   df1h['range_pct'] = (df1h['high'] - df1h['low']) / df1h['close'] * 100
   print(f"\nCandle structure (price action proxies):")
   print(f"  close_pct (0=close@low, 1=close@high): mean={df1h['close_pct'].mean():.3f}
   std={df1h['close_pct'].std():.3f}")
   print(f"  body_pct (body/range ratio):           mean={df1h['body_pct'].mean():.3f}
   std={df1h['body_pct'].std():.3f}")
   print(f"  range_pct (range as % of price):       mean={df1h['range_pct'].mean():.3f}
   std={df1h['range_pct'].std():.3f}")
   print(f"\n  volume mean={df1h['volume'].mean():.0f} std={df1h['volume'].std():.0f}")
   print(f"  vol_ratio (vol/20bar_mean): ", end="")
   df1h['vol_ma'] = df1h['volume'].rolling(20).mean()
   df1h['vol_ratio'] = df1h['volume'] / df1h['vol_ma']
   vr = df1h['vol_ratio'].dropna()
   print(f"mean={vr.mean():.2f} p33={vr.quantile(.33):.2f} p67={vr.quantile(.67):.2f}
   p90={vr.quantile(.90):.2f} p99={vr.quantile(.99):.2f}")

⏺ Done. Here's what was updated in lab/app.py:

  New loader (load_regime_df): reads artifacts/regime_{symbol}.csv from the run folder, parses the UTC index.
  Returns empty DataFrame if the file doesn't exist (backward compatible with RSI4h runs).

  trade_chart_fig now accepts an optional regime_df parameter. When present:
  - Expands to 4 rows (was 3): OHLCV + BB Bands / RSI / Regime / 5m Detail
  - Row 1: BB band lines (upper, mid, lower) drawn as dotted blue/grey overlays, plus BALANCED (green) /
  IMBALANCED (red) background shading via add_vrect
  - Row 3 (new): Step-function traces for structure_num (0=BALANCED, 1=IMBALANCED, filled green) and vol_num
  (0=LOW, 1=NORMAL, 2=HIGH, orange line)
  - When no regime data exists (RSI4h runs), the chart renders exactly as before — 3 rows, no BB bands, no
  shading

  Chart tab: loads regime CSV alongside candles, passes it to trade_chart_fig, shows a caption explaining the
  regime panel axis values.

⏺ Results are in. Let me compile the full picture:

  ---
  Vol regime answer:
  - In the fixed-R baseline (original run): HIGH vol slightly better (+5.62R at 1R TP, n=28)
  - In the TP-at-midband shorts sweep: LOW vol dramatically better (72.2% win, +5.20R, n=18)
  - Neither is reliable — both have n<30, which is statistically noise

  The sweeps reveal the real problem:

  Sweep A — ATR mult × TP at midband:
  The wider the stop, the better — which is the opposite of your hypothesis. Tighter stops destroy R/R because
  the midband is ~1R away regardless of stop width (it's a moving target, not a fixed level). At ATR×0.4 you
  need 18% wins just to break even on midband trades. You never get there. The midband-as-TP idea doesn't work
  because the midband drifts with price during the hold period — it's not a static target.

  Sweep B — Shorts only, TP at midband:
  Shorts are consistently better than the full pool, but still all negative. At ATR×1.5 shorts are at -39R vs
  -244R for all trades — cleaner but not profitable.

  Sweep C — Vol breakdown at ATR×1.5, shorts, TP at midband:

  ┌────────┬──────┬─────────┬───────┐
  │  Vol   │  n   │ total R │ win%  │
  ├────────┼──────┼─────────┼───────┤
  │ LOW    │ 18   │ +5.20   │ 72.2% │
  ├────────┼──────┼─────────┼───────┤
  │ HIGH   │ 27   │ -0.74   │ 40.7% │
  ├────────┼──────┼─────────┼───────┤
  │ NORMAL │ 1122 │ -43.88  │ 46.8% │
  └────────┴──────┴─────────┴───────┘

  The actual diagnosis:

  The strategy has a structural problem, not a parameter problem. On 1h XRP 2022–2026:
  - 1,122 out of 1,190 trades are NORMAL vol — that pool is reliably negative and drowns everything else
  - The long side is broken at every configuration (XRP had extended downtrends in 2022-2023 — BB longs below
  lower band are fading a trend, not reverting)
  - The BB period (20) on 1h bars produces ~2523 BALANCED signals — too many, too noisy

  The one thread worth pursuing: LOW vol BALANCED shorts with TP at midband. 72% win rate needs to be validated
  on more symbols and a wider date range before it means anything. The current n=18 could flip on a single bad
  month.

  Next 3 experiments to run:
  1. Multi-symbol LOW vol BALANCED shorts — run the same config on BTC, ETH, SOL, LINK from 2022 and check if
  the 72% win rate holds or is XRP-specific
  2. BB period sweep on 1h — test bb_period=[30, 50, 100] to reduce NORMAL-vol noise; longer bands produce fewer
   but higher-conviction signals
  3. IMBALANCED regime shorts — your trend-following intuition is probably right; BB upper band in IMBALANCED
  structure may work better as a momentum continuation entry than a mean-reversion short

  Three very clean patterns:                                                                                    
                                                            
  1. Shorts are the entire strategy — longs are negative at every config. The short side of mom|3R is +266R; the
   long side is -73R. The long entry (strong bullish close → buy next open) is essentially fading reversals.
  2. BALANCED wins, IMBALANCED kills — BALANCED structure contributes +230R at mom|3R, IMBALANCED contributes   
  -37R. Every single config shows this split. Trending markets stop out momentum entries.                       
  3. HIGH vol is the edge — HIGH vol thirds contribute +216R at mom|3R vs MED=-44R, LOW=+21R. The momentum close
   signal only works when the market is in an expansionary vol environment. MED vol is a drag everywhere.       
                                                            
  The win rate trade-off is intentional: at 3R TP, 26.6% wins is exactly what you'd need for breakeven on pure  
  ATR stops (breakeven = 1/(1+tp_r) = 25%). Anything above 25% is positive expectancy at 3R — and we're getting
  26.6%, which is slim but real.                                                                                
                                                            
  The two cleanest next experiments:                                                                            
  
  1. Isolate the edge: run mom shorts only, BALANCED regime, HIGH vol third, ATR×1.5, tp=3R — strip out         
  everything that's losing                                  
  2. ATR mult sweep on shorts-only BALANCED: test ×0.75, ×1.0, ×1.25, ×1.5, ×2.0 — the wider stop kept working  
  in the background run, need to find where win rate and DD stabilize                                           
  
  Want me to run those two now?

   import pandas as pd
   import numpy as np
   import sys
   sys.path.insert(0, '.')
   from lab.core.db import load_merged_5m
   from lab.core.resample import resample_ohlcv
   from lab.core.regime import classify_regimes

   df5 = load_merged_5m("/Users/anibalperez/revolutions/backtester/data/backtest.sqlite", "XRPUSDT")
   df5 = df5.loc[df5.index >= pd.Timestamp("2022-01-01", tz="UTC")]
   df1h = resample_ohlcv(df5, "1h").copy()
   df1h = classify_regimes(df1h, atr_period=14, atr_ma_period=50, er_period=20, er_balanced_threshold=0.35)

   df1h['close_pct'] = (df1h['close'] - df1h['low']) / (df1h['high'] - df1h['low']).replace(0, np.nan)
   df1h['body_pct']  = (df1h['close'] - df1h['open']).abs() / (df1h['high'] - df1h['low']).replace(0, np.nan)
   df1h['vol_ratio'] = df1h['volume'] / df1h['volume'].rolling(20, min_periods=10).median()

   p33 = df1h['atr_ratio'].rolling(200, min_periods=50).quantile(0.33)
   p67 = df1h['atr_ratio'].rolling(200, min_periods=50).quantile(0.67)
   df1h['vol_q'] = np.where(df1h['atr_ratio'] < p33, 'LOW',
                   np.where(df1h['atr_ratio'] >= p67, 'HIGH', 'MED'))

   bal   = df1h['structure'] == 'BALANCED'
   hvol  = df1h['vol_q'] == 'HIGH'
   short_close = df1h['close_pct'] < 0.20
   bear_bar    = df1h['close'] < df1h['open']

   print("Signal funnel — how each filter reduces N (short signals only):")
   print(f"  Total 1h bars:                         {len(df1h):>6}")
   print(f"  + bear bar (close < open):             {bear_bar.sum():>6}  ({bear_bar.mean()*100:.1f}%)")
   print(f"  + close_pct < 0.20:                    {(short_close & bear_bar).sum():>6}  ({(short_close &
   bear_bar).mean()*100:.1f}%)")
   print(f"  + vol_ratio > 1.0:                     {(short_close & bear_bar &
   (df1h['vol_ratio']>1.0)).sum():>6}")
   print(f"  + vol_ratio > 1.5:                     {(short_close & bear_bar &
   (df1h['vol_ratio']>1.5)).sum():>6}")
   print(f"  + vol_ratio > 2.0:                     {(short_close & bear_bar &
   (df1h['vol_ratio']>2.0)).sum():>6}")
   print(f"  + body_pct > 0.40:                     {(short_close & bear_bar &
   (df1h['body_pct']>0.40)).sum():>6}")
   print(f"  + body_pct > 0.55:                     {(short_close & bear_bar &
   (df1h['body_pct']>0.55)).sum():>6}")
   base = short_close & bear_bar & (df1h['vol_ratio']>1.0)
   print(f"\n  + BALANCED:                            {(base & bal).sum():>6}")
   print(f"  + BALANCED + HIGH vol:                 {(base & bal & hvol).sum():>6}")
   print(f"  + BALANCED + HIGH vol + body>0.40:     {(base & bal & hvol &
   (df1h['body_pct']>0.40)).sum():>6}")
   print(f"  + BALANCED + HIGH vol + body>0.55:     {(base & bal & hvol &
   (df1h['body_pct']>0.55)).sum():>6}")
   print(f"  + BALANCED + HIGH vol + vol_r>1.5:     {(base & bal & hvol &
   (df1h['vol_ratio']>1.5)).sum():>6}")
   print(f"  + BALANCED + HIGH vol + vol_r>2.0:     {(base & bal & hvol &
   (df1h['vol_ratio']>2.0)).sum():>6}")
   print(f"  + BALANCED + HIGH vol + body>0.4 + vol_r>1.5: {(base & bal & hvol & (df1h['body_pct']>0.40) &
   (df1h['vol_ratio']>1.5)).sum():>6}")
   print(f"  + BALANCED + HIGH vol + body>0.5 + vol_r>2.0: {(base & bal & hvol & (df1h['body_pct']>0.50) &

⏺ Done. Here's what was updated in lab/app.py:

  New loader (load_regime_df): reads artifacts/regime_{symbol}.csv from the run folder, parses the UTC index.
  Returns empty DataFrame if the file doesn't exist (backward compatible with RSI4h runs).

  trade_chart_fig now accepts an optional regime_df parameter. When present:
  - Expands to 4 rows (was 3): OHLCV + BB Bands / RSI / Regime / 5m Detail
  - Row 1: BB band lines (upper, mid, lower) drawn as dotted blue/grey overlays, plus BALANCED (green) /
  IMBALANCED (red) background shading via add_vrect
  - Row 3 (new): Step-function traces for structure_num (0=BALANCED, 1=IMBALANCED, filled green) and vol_num
  (0=LOW, 1=NORMAL, 2=HIGH, orange line)
  - When no regime data exists (RSI4h runs), the chart renders exactly as before — 3 rows, no BB bands, no
  shading

  Chart tab: loads regime CSV alongside candles, passes it to trade_chart_fig, shows a caption explaining the
  regime panel axis values.

⏺ Results are in. Let me compile the full picture:

  ---
  Vol regime answer:
  - In the fixed-R baseline (original run): HIGH vol slightly better (+5.62R at 1R TP, n=28)
  - In the TP-at-midband shorts sweep: LOW vol dramatically better (72.2% win, +5.20R, n=18)
  - Neither is reliable — both have n<30, which is statistically noise

  The sweeps reveal the real problem:

  Sweep A — ATR mult × TP at midband:
  The wider the stop, the better — which is the opposite of your hypothesis. Tighter stops destroy R/R because
  the midband is ~1R away regardless of stop width (it's a moving target, not a fixed level). At ATR×0.4 you
  need 18% wins just to break even on midband trades. You never get there. The midband-as-TP idea doesn't work
  because the midband drifts with price during the hold period — it's not a static target.

  Sweep B — Shorts only, TP at midband:
  Shorts are consistently better than the full pool, but still all negative. At ATR×1.5 shorts are at -39R vs
  -244R for all trades — cleaner but not profitable.

  Sweep C — Vol breakdown at ATR×1.5, shorts, TP at midband:

  ┌────────┬──────┬─────────┬───────┐
  │  Vol   │  n   │ total R │ win%  │
  ├────────┼──────┼─────────┼───────┤
  │ LOW    │ 18   │ +5.20   │ 72.2% │
  ├────────┼──────┼─────────┼───────┤
  │ HIGH   │ 27   │ -0.74   │ 40.7% │
  ├────────┼──────┼─────────┼───────┤
  │ NORMAL │ 1122 │ -43.88  │ 46.8% │
  └────────┴──────┴─────────┴───────┘

  The actual diagnosis:

  The strategy has a structural problem, not a parameter problem. On 1h XRP 2022–2026:
  - 1,122 out of 1,190 trades are NORMAL vol — that pool is reliably negative and drowns everything else
  - The long side is broken at every configuration (XRP had extended downtrends in 2022-2023 — BB longs below
  lower band are fading a trend, not reverting)
  - The BB period (20) on 1h bars produces ~2523 BALANCED signals — too many, too noisy

  The one thread worth pursuing: LOW vol BALANCED shorts with TP at midband. 72% win rate needs to be validated
  on more symbols and a wider date range before it means anything. The current n=18 could flip on a single bad
  month.

  Next 3 experiments to run:
  1. Multi-symbol LOW vol BALANCED shorts — run the same config on BTC, ETH, SOL, LINK from 2022 and check if
  the 72% win rate holds or is XRP-specific
  2. BB period sweep on 1h — test bb_period=[30, 50, 100] to reduce NORMAL-vol noise; longer bands produce fewer
   but higher-conviction signals
  3. IMBALANCED regime shorts — your trend-following intuition is probably right; BB upper band in IMBALANCED
  structure may work better as a momentum continuation entry than a mean-reversion short

  - But the background task showed ATR×1.5 was actually in the old run — the current run only ran ATR×1.0. The
  printout is from the old background job. What you're seeing now:

  From the current run (ATR×1.0 only):

  ┌───────┬──────┬───────┬───────┬─────────┬───────┬────────┬───────┬──────────┬──────────┐

  Three very clean patterns:

  1. Shorts are the entire strategy — longs are negative at every config. The short side of mom|3R is +266R; the
   long side is -73R. The long entry (strong bullish close → buy next open) is essentially fading reversals.
  2. BALANCED wins, IMBALANCED kills — BALANCED structure contributes +230R at mom|3R, IMBALANCED contributes
  -37R. Every single config shows this split. Trending markets stop out momentum entries.
  3. HIGH vol is the edge — HIGH vol thirds contribute +216R at mom|3R vs MED=-44R, LOW=+21R. The momentum close
   signal only works when the market is in an expansionary vol environment. MED vol is a drag everywhere.

  The win rate trade-off is intentional: at 3R TP, 26.6% wins is exactly what you'd need for breakeven on pure
  ATR stops (breakeven = 1/(1+tp_r) = 25%). Anything above 25% is positive expectancy at 3R — and we're getting
  26.6%, which is slim but real.

  The two cleanest next experiments:

  1. Isolate the edge: run mom shorts only, BALANCED regime, HIGH vol third, ATR×1.5, tp=3R — strip out
  everything that's losing
  2. ATR mult sweep on shorts-only BALANCED: test ×0.75, ×1.0, ×1.25, ×1.5, ×2.0 — the wider stop kept working
  in the background run, need to find where win rate and DD stabilize

  Want me to run those two now?

⏺ Done. Here's what was updated in lab/app.py:

  New loader (load_regime_df): reads artifacts/regime_{symbol}.csv from the run folder, parses the UTC index.
  Returns empty DataFrame if the file doesn't exist (backward compatible with RSI4h runs).

  trade_chart_fig now accepts an optional regime_df parameter. When present:
  - Expands to 4 rows (was 3): OHLCV + BB Bands / RSI / Regime / 5m Detail
  - Row 1: BB band lines (upper, mid, lower) drawn as dotted blue/grey overlays, plus BALANCED (green) /
  IMBALANCED (red) background shading via add_vrect
  - Row 3 (new): Step-function traces for structure_num (0=BALANCED, 1=IMBALANCED, filled green) and vol_num
  (0=LOW, 1=NORMAL, 2=HIGH, orange line)
  - When no regime data exists (RSI4h runs), the chart renders exactly as before — 3 rows, no BB bands, no
  shading

  Chart tab: loads regime CSV alongside candles, passes it to trade_chart_fig, shows a caption explaining the
  regime panel axis values.

  The sweeps reveal the real problem:

  Sweep A — ATR mult × TP at midband:
  The wider the stop, the better — which is the opposite of your hypothesis. Tighter stops destroy R/R because
  the midband is ~1R away regardless of stop width (it's a moving target, not a fixed level). At ATR×0.4 you
  need 18% wins just to break even on midband trades. You never get there. The midband-as-TP idea doesn't work
  because the midband drifts with price during the hold period — it's not a static target.

  Sweep B — Shorts only, TP at midband:
  Shorts are consistently better than the full pool, but still all negative. At ATR×1.5 shorts are at -39R vs
  -244R for all trades — cleaner but not profitable.

  The strategy has a structural problem, not a parameter problem. On 1h XRP 2022–2026:

  Three very clean patterns:

  1. Shorts are the entire strategy — longs are negative at every config. The short side of mom|3R is +266R; the
   long side is -73R. The long entry (strong bullish close → buy next open) is essentially fading reversals.
  2. BALANCED wins, IMBALANCED kills — BALANCED structure contributes +230R at mom|3R, IMBALANCED contributes
  -37R. Every single config shows this split. Trending markets stop out momentum entries.
  3. HIGH vol is the edge — HIGH vol thirds contribute +216R at mom|3R vs MED=-44R, LOW=+21R. The momentum close
   signal only works when the market is in an expansionary vol environment. MED vol is a drag everywhere.

  The win rate trade-off is intentional: at 3R TP, 26.6% wins is exactly what you'd need for breakeven on pure
  ATR stops (breakeven = 1/(1+tp_r) = 25%). Anything above 25% is positive expectancy at 3R — and we're getting
  26.6%, which is slim but real.

  The two cleanest next experiments:

  2. ATR mult sweep on shorts-only BALANCED: test ×0.75, ×1.0, ×1.25, ×1.5, ×2.0 — the wider stop kept working
  in the background run, need to find where win rate and DD stabilize

  Want me to run those two now?

  ---
  Sweep 1 — ATR mult (stop distance):

  The wider the stop, the better everything gets — monotonically:

  ┌──────────┬─────┬───────┬─────────┬───────┬──────────┐
  │ ATR mult │ TP  │ win%  │ total R │ maxDD │ DD/trade │
  ├──────────┼─────┼───────┼─────────┼───────┼──────────┤
  │ ×0.75    │ 2R  │ 37.0% │ 22.9    │ 30.2  │ 0.097    │
  ├──────────┼─────┼───────┼─────────┼───────┼──────────┤
  │ ×1.25    │ 2R  │ 38.3% │ 39.3    │ 23.4  │ 0.075    │
  ├──────────┼─────┼───────┼─────────┼───────┼──────────┤
  │ ×1.5     │ 2R  │ 38.6% │ 43.4    │ 17.8  │ 0.057    │
  ├──────────┼─────┼───────┼─────────┼───────┼──────────┤
  │ ×2.0     │ 2R  │ 42.4% │ 80.8    │ 14.5  │ 0.047    │
  ├──────────┼─────┼───────┼─────────┼───────┼──────────┤
  │ ×2.0     │ 3R  │ 32.6% │ 89.8    │ 22.7  │ 0.073    │
  └──────────┴─────┴───────┴─────────┴───────┴──────────┘

  At ATR×2.0, TP=2R: 42% win rate, maxDD=14.5R on 311 trades. That's the best DD/trade ratio (0.047) — meaning
  on average each trade costs 0.047R in drawdown exposure. At 1% risk per trade, that's a 1.4% portfolio max
  drawdown, which is realistic.

  ---
  Sweep 2 — Signal quality (vol_ratio × body_pct):

  The sweet spot is vol_ratio > 1.5, body > 0.55 — tightest signal but:
  - n=274, win%=33.2%, maxDD=12.7R, DD/trade=0.046 (best in sweep)
  - 274 trades over 4 years = ~68/year

  Year-by-year shows the problem: 2024 nearly flat (+1.07R, 25.8% win). That's the outlier year to watch.

  ---
  Two things to carry forward:

  1. Best config so far: mom short | BALANCED | HIGH vol | vol_r>1.5 | body>0.55 | ATR×2.0 | TP=2R — 42% win,
  maxDD=14.5R, ~62 trades/year
  2. 2024 is a red flag — win rate drops to 25.8% in isolation. Before committing to this, that year needs
  understanding (was XRP structure different? sustained uptrend where BALANCED shorts kept getting squeezed?)

  Want to dig into 2024 specifically, or move to validating this config on other symbols first?

   source .venv/bin/activate && python3 - << 'EOF'
   import sys, numpy as np, pandas as pd
   sys.path.insert(0, '.')
   from lab.core.db import load_merged_5m
   from lab.core.resample import resample_ohlcv
   from lab.core.regime import classify_regimes
   from lab.sim.exit import replay_trade_5m
   from lab.sim.entry import tp_price_from_r

   DB     = "/Users/anibalperez/revolutions/backtester/data/backtest.sqlite"
   START  = "2022-01-01"
   SYMS   = ["BTCUSDT", "ETHUSDT", "SOLUSDT", "LINKUSDT", "DOGEUSDT", "XRPUSDT"]

   # Best config
   ATR_MULT   = 2.0
   TP_R       = 2.0
   VOL_R_MIN  = 1.5
   BODY_MIN   = 0.55

   def max_dd(r):
       c = np.cumsum(r); return float(np.max(np.maximum.accumulate(c) - c)) if len(r) else 0.0

   def max_consec_loss(r):
       best = cur = 0
       for p in r:
           cur = cur+1 if p < 0 else 0
           best = max(best, cur)
       return best

   def run_symbol(sym):
       df5 = load_merged_5m(DB, sym)
       df5 = df5.loc[df5.index >= pd.Timestamp(START, tz="UTC")]
       if len(df5) < 5000:
           return None, {}

       df1h = resample_ohlcv(df5, "1h").copy()
       df1h = classify_regimes(df1h, atr_period=14, atr_ma_period=50,
                               er_period=20, er_balanced_threshold=0.35)

       rng = (df1h["high"] - df1h["low"]).replace(0, np.nan)
       df1h["close_pct"] = (df1h["close"] - df1h["low"]) / rng
       df1h["body_pct"]  = (df1h["close"] - df1h["open"]).abs() / rng
       df1h["vol_ratio"] = df1h["volume"] / df1h["volume"].rolling(20, min_periods=10).median()

       atr_r = df1h["atr_ratio"]
       p67   = atr_r.rolling(200, min_periods=50).quantile(0.67)
       p33   = atr_r.rolling(200, min_periods=50).quantile(0.33)
       vol_q = np.where(atr_r >= p67, "HIGH",
               np.where(atr_r < p33, "LOW", "MED")).astype(object)
       vol_q[p67.isna().values] = np.nan
       df1h["vol_q"] = vol_q

       # Collect signals
       sigs = []
       for i in range(60, len(df1h)-1):
           row = df1h.iloc[i]
           if pd.isna(row.get("atr")) or pd.isna(row.get("vol_q")): continue
           if row["structure"] != "BALANCED": continue
           if row["vol_q"] != "HIGH": continue
           if not (row["close_pct"] < 0.20): continue
           if not (row["close"] < row["open"]): continue
           if not (row["vol_ratio"] > VOL_R_MIN): continue
           if not (row["body_pct"] > BODY_MIN): continue
           eb = df1h.iloc[i+1]
           if pd.isna(eb["open"]): continue
           sigs.append({"ts": df1h.index[i+1], "entry_p": float(eb["open"]), "atr": float(row["atr"])})

       # Replay
       all_pnl, by_year = [], {}
       for s in sigs:
           ep = s["entry_p"]
           stop = ep + s["atr"] * ATR_MULT
           risk = stop - ep
           if risk <= 0: continue
           tp_p = tp_price_from_r(ep, risk, -1, TP_R)
           res = replay_trade_5m(df5, s["ts"], -1, ep, stop, tp_p, risk, 3.0,
                                 be_trigger_r=None, be_offset_r=0.0,
                                 skip_entry_bucket_hours=0.0)
           if res:
               all_pnl.append(res.pnl_r)
               yr = s["ts"].year
               by_year.setdefault(yr, []).append(res.pnl_r)

       return np.array(all_pnl), by_year

   print(f"\n{'Symbol':<12} {'n':>5} {'win%':>6} {'avg_R':>7} {'total_R':>8} {'maxDD':>7} {'DD/n':>6}
   {'MCL':>4}")
   print("-" * 65)

   all_results = {}
   for sym in SYMS:
       pnls, by_year = run_symbol(sym)
       if pnls is None or len(pnls) == 0:
           print(f"  {sym:<12}  no data")
           continue
       n    = len(pnls)
       win  = (pnls > 0).mean() * 100
       avg  = pnls.mean()
       tot  = pnls.sum()
       dd   = max_dd(pnls)
       mcl  = max_consec_loss(pnls)
       all_results[sym] = (pnls, by_year)
       print(f"  {sym:<12} {n:>5} {win:>6.1f}% {avg:>7.4f} {tot:>8.2f} {dd:>7.2f} {dd/n:>6.3f} {mcl:>4}")

   # Year-by-year grid
   years = sorted({yr for _, by_year in all_results.values() for yr in by_year})
   print(f"\n--- Year-by-year total_R (ATR×{ATR_MULT}, TP={TP_R}R, shorts, BAL, HIGH vol, vr>1.5, body>0.55)
   ---")
   print(f"{'Symbol':<12}", end="")
   for yr in years: print(f"  {yr}", end="")
   print(f"  {'sum':>7}")
   print("-" * (14 + 7*len(years) + 9))
   for sym, (pnls, by_year) in all_results.items():
       print(f"  {sym:<12}", end="")
       row_tot = 0
       for yr in years:
           r = np.array(by_year.get(yr, []))
           v = r.sum() if len(r) else 0
           row_tot += v
           print(f"  {v:>5.1f}", end="")
       print(f"  {row_tot:>7.1f}")
   print(f"\n  {'ALL':12}", end="")
   grand = 0
   for yr in years:
       v = sum(np.array(by_year.get(yr,[])).sum() for _,(_, by_year) in all_results.items())
       grand += v
       print(f"  {v:>5.1f}", end="")
   print(f"  {grand:>7.1f}")
   EOF

⏺ Done. Here's what was updated in lab/app.py:

  New loader (load_regime_df): reads artifacts/regime_{symbol}.csv from the run folder, parses the UTC index.
  Returns empty DataFrame if the file doesn't exist (backward compatible with RSI4h runs).

  trade_chart_fig now accepts an optional regime_df parameter. When present:
  - Expands to 4 rows (was 3): OHLCV + BB Bands / RSI / Regime / 5m Detail
  - Row 1: BB band lines (upper, mid, lower) drawn as dotted blue/grey overlays, plus BALANCED (green) /
  IMBALANCED (red) background shading via add_vrect
  - Row 3 (new): Step-function traces for structure_num (0=BALANCED, 1=IMBALANCED, filled green) and vol_num
  (0=LOW, 1=NORMAL, 2=HIGH, orange line)
  - When no regime data exists (RSI4h runs), the chart renders exactly as before — 3 rows, no BB bands, no
  shading

  Chart tab: loads regime CSV alongside candles, passes it to trade_chart_fig, shows a caption explaining the
  regime panel axis values.

⏺ Results are in. Let me compile the full picture:

  ---
  Vol regime answer:
  - In the fixed-R baseline (original run): HIGH vol slightly better (+5.62R at 1R TP, n=28)
  - In the TP-at-midband shorts sweep: LOW vol dramatically better (72.2% win, +5.20R, n=18)
  - Neither is reliable — both have n<30, which is statistically noise

  The sweeps reveal the real problem:

  Sweep A — ATR mult × TP at midband:
  The wider the stop, the better — which is the opposite of your hypothesis. Tighter stops destroy R/R because
  the midband is ~1R away regardless of stop width (it's a moving target, not a fixed level). At ATR×0.4 you
  need 18% wins just to break even on midband trades. You never get there. The midband-as-TP idea doesn't work
  because the midband drifts with price during the hold period — it's not a static target.

  Sweep B — Shorts only, TP at midband:
  Shorts are consistently better than the full pool, but still all negative. At ATR×1.5 shorts are at -39R vs
  -244R for all trades — cleaner but not profitable.

  Sweep C — Vol breakdown at ATR×1.5, shorts, TP at midband:

  ┌────────┬──────┬─────────┬───────┐
  │  Vol   │  n   │ total R │ win%  │
  ├────────┼──────┼─────────┼───────┤
  │ LOW    │ 18   │ +5.20   │ 72.2% │
  ├────────┼──────┼─────────┼───────┤
  │ HIGH   │ 27   │ -0.74   │ 40.7% │
  ├────────┼──────┼─────────┼───────┤
  │ NORMAL │ 1122 │ -43.88  │ 46.8% │
  └────────┴──────┴─────────┴───────┘

  The actual diagnosis:

  The strategy has a structural problem, not a parameter problem. On 1h XRP 2022–2026:
  - 1,122 out of 1,190 trades are NORMAL vol — that pool is reliably negative and drowns everything else
  - The long side is broken at every configuration (XRP had extended downtrends in 2022-2023 — BB longs below
  lower band are fading a trend, not reverting)
  - The BB period (20) on 1h bars produces ~2523 BALANCED signals — too many, too noisy

  The one thread worth pursuing: LOW vol BALANCED shorts with TP at midband. 72% win rate needs to be validated
  on more symbols and a wider date range before it means anything. The current n=18 could flip on a single bad
  month.

  Next 3 experiments to run:
  1. Multi-symbol LOW vol BALANCED shorts — run the same config on BTC, ETH, SOL, LINK from 2022 and check if
  the 72% win rate holds or is XRP-specific
  2. BB period sweep on 1h — test bb_period=[30, 50, 100] to reduce NORMAL-vol noise; longer bands produce fewer
   but higher-conviction signals
  3. IMBALANCED regime shorts — your trend-following intuition is probably right; BB upper band in IMBALANCED
  structure may work better as a momentum continuation entry than a mean-reversion short

  of bars because XRP's ATR ratio clusters tightly around 1.0 (p10=0.73, p90=1.35). Almost nothing is LOW or
  HIGH. The fix is quantile thirds at p33/p67 (0.876 / 1.071) giving ~33% each.

  Three very clean patterns:

  1. Shorts are the entire strategy — longs are negative at every config. The short side of mom|3R is +266R; the
   long side is -73R. The long entry (strong bullish close → buy next open) is essentially fading reversals.
  2. BALANCED wins, IMBALANCED kills — BALANCED structure contributes +230R at mom|3R, IMBALANCED contributes
  -37R. Every single config shows this split. Trending markets stop out momentum entries.
  3. HIGH vol is the edge — HIGH vol thirds contribute +216R at mom|3R vs MED=-44R, LOW=+21R. The momentum close
   signal only works when the market is in an expansionary vol environment. MED vol is a drag everywhere.

  The win rate trade-off is intentional: at 3R TP, 26.6% wins is exactly what you'd need for breakeven on pure
  ATR stops (breakeven = 1/(1+tp_r) = 25%). Anything above 25% is positive expectancy at 3R — and we're getting
  26.6%, which is slim but real.

  The two cleanest next experiments:

  1. Isolate the edge: run mom shorts only, BALANCED regime, HIGH vol third, ATR×1.5, tp=3R — strip out
  everything that's losing
  2. ATR mult sweep on shorts-only BALANCED: test ×0.75, ×1.0, ×1.25, ×1.5, ×2.0 — the wider stop kept working
  in the background run, need to find where win rate and DD stabilize

  Want me to run those two now?

 Bash command                                               

   source .venv/bin/activate && python3 - << 'EOF'
   import sys, numpy as np, pandas as pd
   sys.path.insert(0, '.')
   from lab.core.db import load_merged_5m
   from lab.core.resample import resample_ohlcv
   from lab.core.regime import classify_regimes
   from lab.sim.exit import replay_trade_5m
   from lab.sim.entry import tp_price_from_r

   DB    = "/Users/anibalperez/revolutions/backtester/data/backtest.sqlite"
   SYMS  = ["BTCUSDT", "ETHUSDT", "SOLUSDT", "LINKUSDT", "DOGEUSDT", "XRPUSDT"]
   ATR_MULT, TP_R, VOL_R_MIN, BODY_MIN = 2.0, 2.0, 1.5, 0.55

   def max_dd(r):
       c = np.cumsum(r)
       return float(np.max(np.maximum.accumulate(c) - c)) if len(r) else 0.0

   # Aggregate all signals + trades across symbols
   all_signals = []   # {sym, ts, entry_p, atr, pnl, reason, hold_bars}
   regime_by_sym = {} # sym -> df1h (for regime stats)

   for sym in SYMS:
       df5 = load_merged_5m(DB, sym)
       df5 = df5.loc[df5.index >= pd.Timestamp("2022-01-01", tz="UTC")]
       df1h = resample_ohlcv(df5, "1h").copy()
       df1h = classify_regimes(df1h, atr_period=14, atr_ma_period=50,
                               er_period=20, er_balanced_threshold=0.35)
       rng = (df1h["high"] - df1h["low"]).replace(0, np.nan)
       df1h["close_pct"] = (df1h["close"] - df1h["low"]) / rng
       df1h["body_pct"]  = (df1h["close"] - df1h["open"]).abs() / rng
       df1h["vol_ratio"] = df1h["volume"] / df1h["volume"].rolling(20, min_periods=10).median()
       atr_r = df1h["atr_ratio"]
       p67   = atr_r.rolling(200, min_periods=50).quantile(0.67)
       p33   = atr_r.rolling(200, min_periods=50).quantile(0.33)
       vol_q = np.where(atr_r >= p67, "HIGH", np.where(atr_r < p33, "LOW", "MED")).astype(object)
       vol_q[p67.isna().values] = np.nan
       df1h["vol_q"] = vol_q
       regime_by_sym[sym] = df1h

       for i in range(60, len(df1h)-1):
           row = df1h.iloc[i]
           if pd.isna(row.get("atr")) or pd.isna(row.get("vol_q")): continue
           if row["structure"] != "BALANCED": continue
           if row["vol_q"] != "HIGH": continue
           if not (row["close_pct"] < 0.20 and row["close"] < row["open"]): continue
           if not (row["vol_ratio"] > VOL_R_MIN and row["body_pct"] > BODY_MIN): continue
           eb = df1h.iloc[i+1]
           if pd.isna(eb["open"]): continue
           ep = float(eb["open"])
           atr_v = float(row["atr"])
           stop = ep + atr_v * ATR_MULT
           risk = stop - ep
           if risk <= 0: continue
           tp_p = tp_price_from_r(ep, risk, -1, TP_R)
           res = replay_trade_5m(df5, df1h.index[i+1], -1, ep, stop, tp_p, risk, 3.0,
                                 be_trigger_r=None, be_offset_r=0.0, skip_entry_bucket_hours=0.0)
           if res:
               all_signals.append({
                   "sym": sym, "ts": df1h.index[i+1],
                   "year": df1h.index[i+1].year,
                   "month": df1h.index[i+1].to_period("M"),
                   "entry_p": ep, "atr": atr_v,
                   "atr_ratio": float(row["atr_ratio"]),
                   "er": float(row["er"]),
                   "pnl": res.pnl_r, "reason": res.reason, "hold_bars": res.bars,
               })

   df = pd.DataFrame(all_signals)

   # ── 1. Per-year aggregate ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
   print("=== 1. Per-year stats (all symbols combined) ===")
   for yr, g in df.groupby("year"):
       r = g["pnl"].values
       sl_rate = (g["reason"]=="SL").mean()*100
       tp_rate = (g["reason"]=="TP").mean()*100
       print(f"  {yr}  n={len(g):4d}  win={( r>0).mean()*100:5.1f}%  "
             f"avg={r.mean():+.4f}  total={r.sum():+7.2f}  "
             f"SL={sl_rate:.1f}%  TP={tp_rate:.1f}%  "
             f"avg_hold={g['hold_bars'].mean():.0f}bars({g['hold_bars'].mean()*5/60:.1f}h)")

   # ── 2. Regime distribution by year ────────────────────────────────────────
   print("\n=== 2. Regime distribution by year (avg across symbols, 1h bars) ===")
   print(f"  {'year':>6}  {'BALANCED%':>10}  {'HIGH_vol%':>10}  {'atr_ratio_med':>14}  {'er_med':>8}")
   for yr in range(2022, 2027):
       bal_pcts, hvol_pcts, atr_meds, er_meds = [], [], [], []
       for sym, df1h in regime_by_sym.items():
           sub = df1h[df1h.index.year == yr].dropna(subset=["structure","vol_q","atr_ratio","er"])
           if len(sub) < 24: continue
           bal_pcts.append((sub["structure"]=="BALANCED").mean()*100)
           hvol_pcts.append((sub["vol_q"]=="HIGH").mean()*100)
           atr_meds.append(sub["atr_ratio"].median())
           er_meds.append(sub["er"].median())
       if bal_pcts:
           print(f"  {yr:>6}  {np.mean(bal_pcts):>10.1f}%  {np.mean(hvol_pcts):>10.1f}%  "
                 f"{np.mean(atr_meds):>14.3f}  {np.mean(er_meds):>8.3f}")

   # ── 3. Monthly signal count + win rate ────────────────────────────────────
   print("\n=== 3. Monthly signal count + win rate (all symbols) ===")
   print(f"  {'month':>8}  {'n':>4}  {'win%':>6}  {'total_R':>8}  {'SL%':>6}")
   for mo, g in df.groupby("month"):
       r = g["pnl"].values
       sl = (g["reason"]=="SL").mean()*100
       print(f"  {str(mo):>8}  {len(g):>4}  {(r>0).mean()*100:>6.1f}%  {r.sum():>8.2f}  {sl:>6.1f}%")

   # ── 4. 2023 deep-dive — what changed ──────────────────────────────────────
   print("\n=== 4. 2023 vs rest — signal quality metrics ===")
   for lbl, mask in [("2022", df.year==2022), ("2023", df.year==2023),
                     ("2024", df.year==2024), ("2025", df.year==2025)]:
       g = df[mask]
       if len(g) == 0: continue
       print(f"  {lbl}  n={len(g):4d}  "
             f"avg_atr_ratio={g['atr_ratio'].mean():.3f}  "
             f"avg_er={g['er'].mean():.3f}  "
             f"avg_hold={g['hold_bars'].mean():.0f}bars  "
             f"SL%={(g['reason']=='SL').mean()*100:.1f}%")

   # ── 5. 2023 per-symbol breakdown ──────────────────────────────────────────
   print("\n=== 5. 2023 per-symbol breakdown ===")
   g23 = df[df.year==2023]
   for sym, g in g23.groupby("sym"):
       r = g["pnl"].values
       print(f"  {sym:<12}  n={len(g):3d}  win={( r>0).mean()*100:5.1f}%  "
             f"total={r.sum():+7.2f}  SL%={(g['reason']=='SL').mean()*100:.1f}%  "
             f"avg_hold={g['hold_bars'].mean():.0f}b({g['hold_bars'].mean()*5/60:.1f}h)")

      319 +def _add_regime_shading(fig: go.Figure, regime_slice: pd.DataFrame) -> None:                  
      320 +    """                                                                                       
      321 +    Add vertical rectangle shading behind the 4h chart based on structure.                    
      322 +    BALANCED = subtle green, IMBALANCED = subtle red.                                         
      323 +    Only draws transitions (groups contiguous same-structure bars into one vrect).            
      324 +    """                                                                                       
      325 +    if "structure" not in regime_slice.columns or len(regime_slice) == 0:                     
      326 +        return                                                                                
      327 +                                                                                              
      328 +    structure_vals = regime_slice["structure"].values                                         
      329 +    timestamps     = regime_slice.index                                                       
      330 +                                                                                              
      331 +    i = 0                                                                                     
      332 +    while i < len(structure_vals):                                                            
      333 +        s = structure_vals[i]                                                                 
      334 +        if pd.isna(s):                                                                        
      335 +            i += 1                                                                            
      336 +            continue                                                                          
      337 +        j = i + 1                                                                             
      338 +        while j < len(structure_vals) and structure_vals[j] == s:                             
      339 +            j += 1                                                                            
      340 +        t0 = timestamps[i]                                                                    
      341 +        t1 = timestamps[j - 1] + pd.Timedelta(hours=4)  # extend to bar close                 
      342 +        color = "rgba(38,166,154,0.07)" if s == "BALANCED" else "rgba(239,83,80,0.07)"        
      343 +        fig.add_vrect(                                                                        
      344 +            x0=t0, x1=t1,                                                                     
      345 +            fillcolor=color, line_width=0,                                                    
      346 +            layer="below",                                                                    
      347 +            row=1, col=1,                                                                     
      348 +        )                                                                                     
      349 +        i = j                                                                                 
      350 +                                                                                              
      351 +
