⏺ Done. Here's what was updated in lab/app.py:

  New loader (load_regime_df): reads artifacts/regime_{symbol}.csv from the run folder, parses the UTC index.
  Returns empty DataFrame if the file doesn't exist (backward compatible with RSI4h runs).

  trade_chart_fig now accepts an optional regime_df parameter. When present:
  - Expands to 4 rows (was 3): OHLCV + BB Bands / RSI / Regime / 5m Detail
  - Row 1: BB band lines (upper, mid, lower) drawn as dotted blue/grey overlays, plus BALANCED (green) /
  IMBALANCED (red) background shading via add_vrect
  - Row 3 (new): Step-function traces for structure_num (0=BALANCED, 1=IMBALANCED, filled green) and vol_num
  (0=LOW, 1=NORMAL, 2=HIGH, orange line)
  - When no regime data exists (RSI4h runs), the chart renders exactly as before — 3 rows, no BB bands, no
  shading

  Chart tab: loads regime CSV alongside candles, passes it to trade_chart_fig, shows a caption explaining the
  regime panel axis values.

⏺ Results are in. Let me compile the full picture:

  ---
  Vol regime answer:
  - In the fixed-R baseline (original run): HIGH vol slightly better (+5.62R at 1R TP, n=28)
  - In the TP-at-midband shorts sweep: LOW vol dramatically better (72.2% win, +5.20R, n=18)
  - Neither is reliable — both have n<30, which is statistically noise

  The sweeps reveal the real problem:

  Sweep A — ATR mult × TP at midband:
  The wider the stop, the better — which is the opposite of your hypothesis. Tighter stops destroy R/R because
  the midband is ~1R away regardless of stop width (it's a moving target, not a fixed level). At ATR×0.4 you
  need 18% wins just to break even on midband trades. You never get there. The midband-as-TP idea doesn't work
  because the midband drifts with price during the hold period — it's not a static target.

  Sweep B — Shorts only, TP at midband:
  Shorts are consistently better than the full pool, but still all negative. At ATR×1.5 shorts are at -39R vs
  -244R for all trades — cleaner but not profitable.

  Sweep C — Vol breakdown at ATR×1.5, shorts, TP at midband:

  ┌────────┬──────┬─────────┬───────┐
  │  Vol   │  n   │ total R │ win%  │
  ├────────┼──────┼─────────┼───────┤
  │ LOW    │ 18   │ +5.20   │ 72.2% │
  ├────────┼──────┼─────────┼───────┤
  │ HIGH   │ 27   │ -0.74   │ 40.7% │
  ├────────┼──────┼─────────┼───────┤
  │ NORMAL │ 1122 │ -43.88  │ 46.8% │
  └────────┴──────┴─────────┴───────┘

  The actual diagnosis:

  The strategy has a structural problem, not a parameter problem. On 1h XRP 2022–2026:
  - 1,122 out of 1,190 trades are NORMAL vol — that pool is reliably negative and drowns everything else
  - The long side is broken at every configuration (XRP had extended downtrends in 2022-2023 — BB longs below
  lower band are fading a trend, not reverting)
  - The BB period (20) on 1h bars produces ~2523 BALANCED signals — too many, too noisy

  The one thread worth pursuing: LOW vol BALANCED shorts with TP at midband. 72% win rate needs to be validated
  on more symbols and a wider date range before it means anything. The current n=18 could flip on a single bad
  month.

  Next 3 experiments to run:
  1. Multi-symbol LOW vol BALANCED shorts — run the same config on BTC, ETH, SOL, LINK from 2022 and check if
  the 72% win rate holds or is XRP-specific
  2. BB period sweep on 1h — test bb_period=[30, 50, 100] to reduce NORMAL-vol noise; longer bands produce fewer
   but higher-conviction signals
  3. IMBALANCED regime shorts — your trend-following intuition is probably right; BB upper band in IMBALANCED
  structure may work better as a momentum continuation entry than a mean-reversion short

  Three very clean patterns:

  1. Shorts are the entire strategy — longs are negative at every config. The short side of mom|3R is +266R; the
   long side is -73R. The long entry (strong bullish close → buy next open) is essentially fading reversals.
  2. BALANCED wins, IMBALANCED kills — BALANCED structure contributes +230R at mom|3R, IMBALANCED contributes
  -37R. Every single config shows this split. Trending markets stop out momentum entries.
  3. HIGH vol is the edge — HIGH vol thirds contribute +216R at mom|3R vs MED=-44R, LOW=+21R. The momentum close
   signal only works when the market is in an expansionary vol environment. MED vol is a drag everywhere.

  The win rate trade-off is intentional: at 3R TP, 26.6% wins is exactly what you'd need for breakeven on pure
  ATR stops (breakeven = 1/(1+tp_r) = 25%). Anything above 25% is positive expectancy at 3R — and we're getting
  26.6%, which is slim but real.

  The two cleanest next experiments:

  1. Isolate the edge: run mom shorts only, BALANCED regime, HIGH vol third, ATR×1.5, tp=3R — strip out
  everything that's losing
  2. ATR mult sweep on shorts-only BALANCED: test ×0.75, ×1.0, ×1.25, ×1.5, ×2.0 — the wider stop kept working
  in the background run, need to find where win rate and DD stabilize

  Want me to run those two now?

⏺ Done. Here's what was updated in lab/app.py:

  New loader (load_regime_df): reads artifacts/regime_{symbol}.csv from the run folder, parses the UTC index.
  Returns empty DataFrame if the file doesn't exist (backward compatible with RSI4h runs).

  trade_chart_fig now accepts an optional regime_df parameter. When present:
  - Expands to 4 rows (was 3): OHLCV + BB Bands / RSI / Regime / 5m Detail
  - Row 1: BB band lines (upper, mid, lower) drawn as dotted blue/grey overlays, plus BALANCED (green) /
  IMBALANCED (red) background shading via add_vrect
  - Row 3 (new): Step-function traces for structure_num (0=BALANCED, 1=IMBALANCED, filled green) and vol_num
  (0=LOW, 1=NORMAL, 2=HIGH, orange line)
  - When no regime data exists (RSI4h runs), the chart renders exactly as before — 3 rows, no BB bands, no
  shading

  Chart tab: loads regime CSV alongside candles, passes it to trade_chart_fig, shows a caption explaining the
  regime panel axis values.

⏺ Results are in. Let me compile the full picture:

  ---
  Vol regime answer:
  - In the fixed-R baseline (original run): HIGH vol slightly better (+5.62R at 1R TP, n=28)
  - In the TP-at-midband shorts sweep: LOW vol dramatically better (72.2% win, +5.20R, n=18)
  - Neither is reliable — both have n<30, which is statistically noise

  The sweeps reveal the real problem:

  Sweep A — ATR mult × TP at midband:
  The wider the stop, the better — which is the opposite of your hypothesis. Tighter stops destroy R/R because
  the midband is ~1R away regardless of stop width (it's a moving target, not a fixed level). At ATR×0.4 you
  need 18% wins just to break even on midband trades. You never get there. The midband-as-TP idea doesn't work
  because the midband drifts with price during the hold period — it's not a static target.

  Sweep B — Shorts only, TP at midband:
  Shorts are consistently better than the full pool, but still all negative. At ATR×1.5 shorts are at -39R vs
  -244R for all trades — cleaner but not profitable.

  Sweep C — Vol breakdown at ATR×1.5, shorts, TP at midband:

  ┌────────┬──────┬─────────┬───────┐
  │  Vol   │  n   │ total R │ win%  │
  ├────────┼──────┼─────────┼───────┤
  │ LOW    │ 18   │ +5.20   │ 72.2% │
  ├────────┼──────┼─────────┼───────┤
  │ HIGH   │ 27   │ -0.74   │ 40.7% │
  ├────────┼──────┼─────────┼───────┤
  │ NORMAL │ 1122 │ -43.88  │ 46.8% │
  └────────┴──────┴─────────┴───────┘

  The actual diagnosis:

  The strategy has a structural problem, not a parameter problem. On 1h XRP 2022–2026:
  - 1,122 out of 1,190 trades are NORMAL vol — that pool is reliably negative and drowns everything else
  - The long side is broken at every configuration (XRP had extended downtrends in 2022-2023 — BB longs below
  lower band are fading a trend, not reverting)
  - The BB period (20) on 1h bars produces ~2523 BALANCED signals — too many, too noisy

  The one thread worth pursuing: LOW vol BALANCED shorts with TP at midband. 72% win rate needs to be validated
  on more symbols and a wider date range before it means anything. The current n=18 could flip on a single bad
  month.

  Next 3 experiments to run:
  1. Multi-symbol LOW vol BALANCED shorts — run the same config on BTC, ETH, SOL, LINK from 2022 and check if
  the 72% win rate holds or is XRP-specific
  2. BB period sweep on 1h — test bb_period=[30, 50, 100] to reduce NORMAL-vol noise; longer bands produce fewer
   but higher-conviction signals
  3. IMBALANCED regime shorts — your trend-following intuition is probably right; BB upper band in IMBALANCED
  structure may work better as a momentum continuation entry than a mean-reversion short

      import sys, numpy as np, pandas as pd…)
  ⎿  Running…                                                                                                   
                                                                                                              
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
 Bash command                                               

   source .venv/bin/activate && python3 - << 'EOF'
   import sys, numpy as np, pandas as pd
   sys.path.insert(0, '.')
   from lab.core.db import load_merged_5m
   from lab.core.resample import resample_ohlcv
   from lab.core.regime import classify_regimes
   from lab.sim.exit import replay_trade_5m
   from lab.sim.entry import tp_price_from_r

   DB    = "/Users/anibalperez/revolutions/backtester/data/backtest.sqlite"
   SYMS  = ["BTCUSDT","ETHUSDT","SOLUSDT","LINKUSDT","DOGEUSDT","XRPUSDT"]
   ATR_MULT, TP_R, VOL_R_MIN, BODY_MIN = 2.0, 2.0, 1.5, 0.55

   def max_dd(r):
       c = np.cumsum(r)
       return float(np.max(np.maximum.accumulate(c) - c)) if len(r) else 0.0

   # Build BTC daily SMA200 as the macro trend filter
   # Only take shorts when asset's own daily close < 200D SMA
   # This is NO-LOOKAHEAD: SMA at bar i uses bars 0..i, entry at bar i+1

   all_trades = []  # full record for analysis

   for sym in SYMS:
       df5 = load_merged_5m(DB, sym)
       df5 = df5.loc[df5.index >= pd.Timestamp("2022-01-01", tz="UTC")]

       # Daily SMA200 for this asset (trend context filter)
       df1d = resample_ohlcv(df5, "1D").copy()
       df1d["sma200d"] = df1d["close"].rolling(200, min_periods=100).mean()
       df1d["below_sma200d"] = df1d["close"] < df1d["sma200d"]
       # Forward-fill daily value to 1h bars (use previous day's close signal)
       sma_daily = df1d["below_sma200d"].shift(1).reindex(
           pd.date_range(df5.index[0], df5.index[-1], freq="1h", tz="UTC"),
           method="ffill"
       )

       df1h = resample_ohlcv(df5, "1h").copy()
       df1h = classify_regimes(df1h, atr_period=14, atr_ma_period=50,
                               er_period=20, er_balanced_threshold=0.35)
       rng = (df1h["high"] - df1h["low"]).replace(0, np.nan)
       df1h["close_pct"] = (df1h["close"] - df1h["low"]) / rng
       df1h["body_pct"]  = (df1h["close"] - df1h["open"]).abs() / rng
       df1h["vol_ratio"] = df1h["volume"] / df1h["volume"].rolling(20, min_periods=10).median()
       atr_r = df1h["atr_ratio"]
       p67   = atr_r.rolling(200, min_periods=50).quantile(0.67)
       p33   = atr_r.rolling(200, min_periods=50).quantile(0.33)
       vol_q = np.where(atr_r >= p67, "HIGH", np.where(atr_r < p33, "LOW", "MED")).astype(object)
       vol_q[p67.isna().values] = np.nan
       df1h["vol_q"] = vol_q

       for i in range(60, len(df1h)-1):
           row = df1h.iloc[i]
           if pd.isna(row.get("atr")) or pd.isna(row.get("vol_q")): continue
           if row["structure"] != "BALANCED": continue
           if row["vol_q"] != "HIGH": continue
           if not (row["close_pct"] < 0.20 and row["close"] < row["open"]): continue
           if not (row["vol_ratio"] > VOL_R_MIN and row["body_pct"] > BODY_MIN): continue
           eb = df1h.iloc[i+1]
           if pd.isna(eb["open"]): continue
           ts = df1h.index[i+1]
           ep = float(eb["open"])
           atr_v = float(row["atr"])
           stop = ep + atr_v * ATR_MULT
           risk = stop - ep
           if risk <= 0: continue
           tp_p = tp_price_from_r(ep, risk, -1, TP_R)
           res = replay_trade_5m(df5, ts, -1, ep, stop, tp_p, risk, 3.0,
                                 be_trigger_r=None, be_offset_r=0.0, skip_entry_bucket_hours=0.0)
           if not res: continue

           # Was the macro trend filter satisfied?
           below_200d = bool(sma_daily.get(ts, False))

           all_trades.append({
               "sym": sym, "year": ts.year, "month": ts.to_period("M"),
               "pnl": res.pnl_r, "reason": res.reason,
               "below_200d": below_200d,
           })

   df = pd.DataFrame(all_trades)

   # ── Compare: all trades vs filtered (below 200D SMA only) ─────────────────
   print("=== Filter impact: close < 200D SMA ===")
   print(f"\n  Unfiltered (all {len(df)} trades):")
   r = df["pnl"].values
   print(f"    win={( r>0).mean()*100:.1f}%  avg={r.mean():+.4f}  total={r.sum():+.2f}
   maxDD={max_dd(r):.2f}")

   filt = df[df["below_200d"]]
   r_f = filt["pnl"].values
   print(f"\n  Filtered — below 200D SMA ({len(filt)} trades, {len(filt)/len(df)*100:.0f}% kept):")
   print(f"    win={( r_f>0).mean()*100:.1f}%  avg={r_f.mean():+.4f}  total={r_f.sum():+.2f}
   maxDD={max_dd(r_f):.2f}")

   excl = df[~df["below_200d"]]
   r_e = excl["pnl"].values
   print(f"\n  Excluded — above 200D SMA ({len(excl)} trades):")
   print(f"    win={( r_e>0).mean()*100:.1f}%  avg={r_e.mean():+.4f}  total={r_e.sum():+.2f}
   maxDD={max_dd(r_e):.2f}")

   print(f"\n=== Year-by-year: unfiltered vs filtered ===")
   print(f"  {'year':>6}  {'all_n':>6}  {'all_R':>7}  {'filt_n':>7}  {'filt_R':>7}  {'filt_win%':>10}
   {'trades_kept%':>13}")
   for yr in sorted(df["year"].unique()):
       ga = df[df["year"]==yr]["pnl"].values
       gf = filt[filt["year"]==yr]["pnl"].values
       kept_pct = len(gf)/len(ga)*100 if len(ga) else 0
       print(f"  {yr:>6}  {len(ga):>6}  {ga.sum():>7.2f}  {len(gf):>7}  "
             f"{gf.sum() if len(gf) else 0:>7.2f}  "
             f"{(gf>0).mean()*100 if len(gf) else 0:>10.1f}%  {kept_pct:>12.0f}%")

   print(f"\n=== Per-symbol with filter ===")
   print(f"  {'sym':<12}  {'n_filt':>7}  {'win%':>6}  {'avg_R':>7}  {'total_R':>8}  {'maxDD':>7}")
   for sym, g in filt.groupby("sym"):
       r = g["pnl"].values
       print(f"  {sym:<12}  {len(r):>7}  {(r>0).mean()*100:>6.1f}%  {r.mean():>7.4f}  {r.sum():>8.2f}
   {max_dd(r):>7.2f}")

⏺ Done. Here's what was updated in lab/app.py:

  New loader (load_regime_df): reads artifacts/regime_{symbol}.csv from the run folder, parses the UTC index.
  Returns empty DataFrame if the file doesn't exist (backward compatible with RSI4h runs).

  trade_chart_fig now accepts an optional regime_df parameter. When present:
  - Expands to 4 rows (was 3): OHLCV + BB Bands / RSI / Regime / 5m Detail
  - Row 1: BB band lines (upper, mid, lower) drawn as dotted blue/grey overlays, plus BALANCED (green) /
  IMBALANCED (red) background shading via add_vrect
  - Row 3 (new): Step-function traces for structure_num (0=BALANCED, 1=IMBALANCED, filled green) and vol_num
  (0=LOW, 1=NORMAL, 2=HIGH, orange line)
  - When no regime data exists (RSI4h runs), the chart renders exactly as before — 3 rows, no BB bands, no
  shading

  Chart tab: loads regime CSV alongside candles, passes it to trade_chart_fig, shows a caption explaining the
  regime panel axis values.

⏺ Here's the diagnosis. Now building the two sweeps directly.

  Key findings from the data:
  - HIGH vol is the only regime with positive R, but only n=28 (too small to trust alone)
  - Short/Long asymmetry is massive: shorts are breakeven-to-positive across all TPs, longs are deeply negative
  — the ATR stop is 1.23× wider than the half-band, meaning you're risking more than the natural reversal target
   distance
  - TP at midband makes it worse at current stop sizing because midband is only ~1.07R away — that's below the
  fee threshold to be useful
  - To make midband = 1.5R, you need ATR mult ~0.88; for 2.0R you need ~0.66 — the stop needs to come in
  significantly
  - Two sweeps worth running: (1) ATR mult tightness with TP at midband, (2) Shorts-only with same

⏺ Results are in. Let me compile the full picture:

  ---
  Vol regime answer:
  - In the fixed-R baseline (original run): HIGH vol slightly better (+5.62R at 1R TP, n=28)
  - In the TP-at-midband shorts sweep: LOW vol dramatically better (72.2% win, +5.20R, n=18)
  - Neither is reliable — both have n<30, which is statistically noise

  The sweeps reveal the real problem:

  Sweep A — ATR mult × TP at midband:
  The wider the stop, the better — which is the opposite of your hypothesis. Tighter stops destroy R/R because
  the midband is ~1R away regardless of stop width (it's a moving target, not a fixed level). At ATR×0.4 you
  need 18% wins just to break even on midband trades. You never get there. The midband-as-TP idea doesn't work
  because the midband drifts with price during the hold period — it's not a static target.

  Sweep B — Shorts only, TP at midband:
  Shorts are consistently better than the full pool, but still all negative. At ATR×1.5 shorts are at -39R vs
  -244R for all trades — cleaner but not profitable.

  Sweep C — Vol breakdown at ATR×1.5, shorts, TP at midband:

  ┌────────┬──────┬─────────┬───────┐
  │  Vol   │  n   │ total R │ win%  │
  ├────────┼──────┼─────────┼───────┤

  ├────────┼──────┼─────────┼───────┤
  │ HIGH   │ 27   │ -0.74   │ 40.7% │
  ├────────┼──────┼─────────┼───────┤
  │ NORMAL │ 1122 │ -43.88  │ 46.8% │
  └────────┴──────┴─────────┴───────┘

  The actual diagnosis:

  The strategy has a structural problem, not a parameter problem. On 1h XRP 2022–2026:
  - 1,122 out of 1,190 trades are NORMAL vol — that pool is reliably negative and drowns everything else
  - The long side is broken at every configuration (XRP had extended downtrends in 2022-2023 — BB longs below
  lower band are fading a trend, not reverting)
  - The BB period (20) on 1h bars produces ~2523 BALANCED signals — too many, too noisy

  The one thread worth pursuing: LOW vol BALANCED shorts with TP at midband. 72% win rate needs to be validated
  on more symbols and a wider date range before it means anything. The current n=18 could flip on a single bad
  month.

  Next 3 experiments to run:
  1. Multi-symbol LOW vol BALANCED shorts — run the same config on BTC, ETH, SOL, LINK from 2022 and check if
  the 72% win rate holds or is XRP-specific
  2. BB period sweep on 1h — test bb_period=[30, 50, 100] to reduce NORMAL-vol noise; longer bands produce fewer
   but higher-conviction signals
  3. IMBALANCED regime shorts — your trend-following intuition is probably right; BB upper band in IMBALANCED
  structure may work better as a momentum continuation entry than a mean-reversion short

⏺ Here's the complete picture:                                                                                  
                                                                                                                
  ---                                                                                                           
  Root cause: macro trend.                                                                                      
                                                                                                                
  The strategy is a short-biased momentum signal (bearish close, strong body, elevated volume). In a sustained  
  bull market — when the asset is trading above its 200D SMA — every BALANCED regime pullback has an upward     
  drift that stops out shorts before they reach 2R. The regime filter (BALANCED + HIGH vol) only looks at local
  structure. It can't see the macro context.                                                                    
                                                            
  What happened month by month:                                                                                 
  - 2023 Jan–May: BTC crossed above 200D SMA for the first time since early 2022 (+39% in January alone). Every
  short entry was being stopped out by the recovery drift. SL rate hit 87.8% in April 2023 — almost every single
   trade stopped out.                                                                                           
  - The exact same pattern hit Feb 2024 (+42.6% BTC month) and Nov 2024 (+37.2%) — both show up as the two worst
   months of 2024.                                                                                              
                                                                                                                
  Filter impact: asset close < 200D SMA
                                                                                                                
  ┌────────────────┬────────┬───────┬─────────┬───────┐     
  │                │ Trades │ Win%  │ Total R │ MaxDD │                                                         
  ├────────────────┼────────┼───────┼─────────┼───────┤                                                         
  │ Unfiltered     │ 1,910  │ 37.7% │ +226.5  │ 39.4  │
  ├────────────────┼────────┼───────┼─────────┼───────┤                                                         
  │ Below 200D SMA │ 920    │ 39.8% │ +165.9  │ 31.9  │     
  ├────────────────┼────────┼───────┼─────────┼───────┤                                                         
  │ Above 200D SMA │ 990    │ 35.9% │ +60.7   │ 34.8  │
  └────────────────┴────────┴───────┴─────────┴───────┘                                                         
                                                            
  The filter cuts trades in half (1,910 → 920) but keeps 73% of the R. Win rate goes from 37.7% to 39.8%, maxDD 
  drops from 39.4 to 31.9R.                                 
                                                                                                                
  But there's a problem: ETH flips negative (-18.76R) and SOL stays weak. The filter helps most assets but isn't
   clean enough on its own. 2023 goes from -12R to -4R — better but still negative.
                                                                                                                
  The filter isn't wrong, it's insufficient. The 200D SMA is too slow — it was already above the SMA when things
   were bad. What's actually needed is: only short during local downtrends or corrective phases, not just "asset
   below 200D SMA." The 200D SMA keeps ETH/SOL filtered out during good periods too (they were below 200D in    
  2023 but choppy, not cleanly trending down).              

  The real fix is an additional filter: short-term trend confirmation. Before taking a short signal, confirm    
  that the asset is actually in a local downswing — not just globally below a slow MA. Candidates:
                                                                                                                
  1. Price below its own 4h 50-bar SMA at signal time (50 × 4h = 200h of local trend context)                   
  2. Daily close making lower highs over last 5 days (structural breakdown)
  3. Both: below 200D SMA AND below 4h 50-bar SMA (dual-TF confirmation)                                        
                                                                                                                
  Want to test that combination?

   import sys, numpy as np, pandas as pd
   sys.path.insert(0, '.')
   from lab.core.db import load_merged_5m
   from lab.core.resample import resample_ohlcv
   from lab.core.regime import classify_regimes
   from lab.sim.exit import replay_trade_5m
   from lab.sim.entry import tp_price_from_r

   DB       = "/Users/anibalperez/revolutions/backtester/data/backtest.sqlite"
   SYMS     = ["BTCUSDT","ETHUSDT","SOLUSDT","LINKUSDT","DOGEUSDT","XRPUSDT"]
   ATR_MULT = 2.0
   TP_SWEEP = [1.0, 1.5, 2.0, 2.5, 3.0, 4.0, 5.0]

   def max_dd(r):
       c = np.cumsum(r)
       return float(np.max(np.maximum.accumulate(c) - c)) if len(r) else 0.0

   # ── Collect all signals once ───────────────────────────────────────────────
   print("Loading signals...")
   signals = []   # {sym, ts, entry_p, atr}
   for sym in SYMS:
       df5 = load_merged_5m(DB, sym)
       df5 = df5.loc[df5.index >= pd.Timestamp("2022-01-01", tz="UTC")]
       df1h = resample_ohlcv(df5, "1h").copy()
       df1h = classify_regimes(df1h, atr_period=14, atr_ma_period=50,
                               er_period=20, er_balanced_threshold=0.35)
       rng = (df1h["high"] - df1h["low"]).replace(0, np.nan)
       df1h["close_pct"] = (df1h["close"] - df1h["low"]) / rng
       df1h["body_pct"]  = (df1h["close"] - df1h["open"]).abs() / rng
       df1h["vol_ratio"] = df1h["volume"] / df1h["volume"].rolling(20, min_periods=10).median()
       atr_r = df1h["atr_ratio"]
       p67 = atr_r.rolling(200, min_periods=50).quantile(0.67)
       p33 = atr_r.rolling(200, min_periods=50).quantile(0.33)
       vol_q = np.where(atr_r >= p67, "HIGH", np.where(atr_r < p33, "LOW", "MED")).astype(object)
       vol_q[p67.isna().values] = np.nan
       df1h["vol_q"] = vol_q

       for i in range(60, len(df1h)-1):
           row = df1h.iloc[i]
           if pd.isna(row.get("atr")) or pd.isna(row.get("vol_q")): continue
           if row["structure"] != "BALANCED": continue
           if row["vol_q"] != "HIGH": continue
           if not (row["close_pct"] < 0.20 and row["close"] < row["open"]): continue
           if not (row["vol_ratio"] > 1.5 and row["body_pct"] > 0.55): continue
           eb = df1h.iloc[i+1]
           if pd.isna(eb["open"]): continue
           signals.append({
               "sym": sym, "df5": df5,
               "ts": df1h.index[i+1],
               "entry_p": float(eb["open"]),
               "atr": float(row["atr"]),
               "year": df1h.index[i+1].year,
           })
       print(f"  {sym}: {sum(1 for s in signals if s['sym']==sym)} signals")

   print(f"  Total: {len(signals)} signals\n")

   # ── Sweep TP ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
   # results[tp][sym] = list of pnl
   from collections import defaultdict
   results = {}   # tp -> {sym -> [pnl], year -> [pnl]}

   for tp_r in TP_SWEEP:
       sym_pnl  = defaultdict(list)
       year_pnl = defaultdict(list)
       for s in signals:
           ep   = s["entry_p"]
           stop = ep + s["atr"] * ATR_MULT
           risk = stop - ep
           if risk <= 0: continue
           tp_p = tp_price_from_r(ep, risk, -1, tp_r)
           res = replay_trade_5m(s["df5"], s["ts"], -1, ep, stop, tp_p, risk, 3.0,
                                 be_trigger_r=None, be_offset_r=0.0,
                                 skip_entry_bucket_hours=0.0)
           if res:
               sym_pnl[s["sym"]].append(res.pnl_r)
               year_pnl[s["year"]].append(res.pnl_r)
       results[tp_r] = {"sym": sym_pnl, "year": year_pnl}

   # ── Print: aggregate ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
   YEARS = [2022, 2023, 2024, 2025]

   print(f"{'TP':>5}  {'n':>5}  {'win%':>6}  {'avg_R':>7}  {'total_R':>8}  {'maxDD':>7}  {'DD/n':>6}",
   end="")
   for yr in YEARS: print(f"  {yr}", end="")
   print()
   print("-" * 90)

   for tp_r in TP_SWEEP:
       all_pnl = [p for plist in results[tp_r]["sym"].values() for p in plist]
       r = np.array(all_pnl)
       n = len(r)
       yr_tots = [round(np.array(results[tp_r]["year"].get(yr, [])).sum(), 1) for yr in YEARS]
       print(f"{tp_r:>5.1f}  {n:>5}  {(r>0).mean()*100:>6.1f}%  {r.mean():>7.4f}  "
             f"{r.sum():>8.2f}  {max_dd(r):>7.2f}  {max_dd(r)/n:>6.3f}", end="")
       for v in yr_tots: print(f"  {v:>5.1f}", end="")
       print()

   # ── Print: per-symbol per-TP ──────────────────────────────────────────────
   print(f"\n{'Per-symbol total R by TP':}")
   print(f"  {'symbol':<12}", end="")
   for tp in TP_SWEEP: print(f"  {tp:>5.1f}R", end="")
   print()
   print("  " + "-" * (14 + 8*len(TP_SWEEP)))
   for sym in SYMS:
       print(f"  {sym:<12}", end="")
       for tp in TP_SWEEP:
           plist = results[tp]["sym"].get(sym, [])
           v = np.array(plist).sum() if plist else 0
           print(f"  {v:>6.1f}", end="")
       print()

   # ── Win rate by TP per symbol ─────────────────────────────────────────────
   print(f"\n{'Per-symbol win% by TP':}")
   print(f"  {'symbol':<12}", end="")
   for tp in TP_SWEEP: print(f"  {tp:>5.1f}R", end="")
   print()
   print("  " + "-" * (14 + 8*len(TP_SWEEP)))
   for sym in SYMS:
       print(f"  {sym:<12}", end="")
       for tp in TP_SWEEP:
           plist = results[tp]["sym"].get(sym, [])
           r = np.array(plist)
           v = (r > 0).mean() * 100 if len(r) else 0
           print(f"  {v:>6.1f}", end="")
       print()

   # ── MaxDD by TP ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
   print(f"\n{'MaxDD by TP (all symbols combined)':}")
   print(f"  {'TP':>5}  {'maxDD':>7}  {'DD/n':>6}  {'best_yr':>8}  {'worst_yr':>9}")
   for tp in TP_SWEEP:
       all_pnl = [p for plist in results[tp]["sym"].values() for p in plist]
       r = np.array(all_pnl)
       yr_tots = {yr: np.array(results[tp]["year"].get(yr,[])).sum() for yr in YEARS}
       best  = max(yr_tots, key=yr_tots.get)
       worst = min(yr_tots, key=yr_tots.get)
       print(f"  {tp:>5.1f}  {max_dd(r):>7.2f}  {max_dd(r)/len(r):>6.3f}  "
             f"{best}:{yr_tots[best]:>+6.1f}  {worst}:{yr_tots[worst]:>+6.1f}")

⏺ Done. Here's what was updated in lab/app.py:

  New loader (load_regime_df): reads artifacts/regime_{symbol}.csv from the run folder, parses the UTC index.
  Returns empty DataFrame if the file doesn't exist (backward compatible with RSI4h runs).

  trade_chart_fig now accepts an optional regime_df parameter. When present:
  - Expands to 4 rows (was 3): OHLCV + BB Bands / RSI / Regime / 5m Detail
  - Row 1: BB band lines (upper, mid, lower) drawn as dotted blue/grey overlays, plus BALANCED (green) /
  IMBALANCED (red) background shading via add_vrect
  - Row 3 (new): Step-function traces for structure_num (0=BALANCED, 1=IMBALANCED, filled green) and vol_num
  (0=LOW, 1=NORMAL, 2=HIGH, orange line)
  - When no regime data exists (RSI4h runs), the chart renders exactly as before — 3 rows, no BB bands, no
  shading

  Chart tab: loads regime CSV alongside candles, passes it to trade_chart_fig, shows a caption explaining the
  regime panel axis values.

⏺ Results are in. Let me compile the full picture:

  ---
  Vol regime answer:
  - In the fixed-R baseline (original run): HIGH vol slightly better (+5.62R at 1R TP, n=28)
  - In the TP-at-midband shorts sweep: LOW vol dramatically better (72.2% win, +5.20R, n=18)
  - Neither is reliable — both have n<30, which is statistically noise

  The sweeps reveal the real problem:

  Sweep A — ATR mult × TP at midband:
  The wider the stop, the better — which is the opposite of your hypothesis. Tighter stops destroy R/R because
  the midband is ~1R away regardless of stop width (it's a moving target, not a fixed level). At ATR×0.4 you
  need 18% wins just to break even on midband trades. You never get there. The midband-as-TP idea doesn't work
  because the midband drifts with price during the hold period — it's not a static target.

  Sweep B — Shorts only, TP at midband:
  Shorts are consistently better than the full pool, but still all negative. At ATR×1.5 shorts are at -39R vs
  -244R for all trades — cleaner but not profitable.

  Sweep C — Vol breakdown at ATR×1.5, shorts, TP at midband:

  ┌────────┬──────┬─────────┬───────┐
  │  Vol   │  n   │ total R │ win%  │
  ├────────┼──────┼─────────┼───────┤
  │ LOW    │ 18   │ +5.20   │ 72.2% │
  ├────────┼──────┼─────────┼───────┤
  │ HIGH   │ 27   │ -0.74   │ 40.7% │
  ├────────┼──────┼─────────┼───────┤
  │ NORMAL │ 1122 │ -43.88  │ 46.8% │
  └────────┴──────┴─────────┴───────┘

  The actual diagnosis:

  The strategy has a structural problem, not a parameter problem. On 1h XRP 2022–2026:
  - 1,122 out of 1,190 trades are NORMAL vol — that pool is reliably negative and drowns everything else
  - The long side is broken at every configuration (XRP had extended downtrends in 2022-2023 — BB longs below
  lower band are fading a trend, not reverting)
  - The BB period (20) on 1h bars produces ~2523 BALANCED signals — too many, too noisy

  The one thread worth pursuing: LOW vol BALANCED shorts with TP at midband. 72% win rate needs to be validated
  on more symbols and a wider date range before it means anything. The current n=18 could flip on a single bad
  month.

  Next 3 experiments to run:
  1. Multi-symbol LOW vol BALANCED shorts — run the same config on BTC, ETH, SOL, LINK from 2022 and check if
  the 72% win rate holds or is XRP-specific
  2. BB period sweep on 1h — test bb_period=[30, 50, 100] to reduce NORMAL-vol noise; longer bands produce fewer
   but higher-conviction signals
  3. IMBALANCED regime shorts — your trend-following intuition is probably right; BB upper band in IMBALANCED
  structure may work better as a momentum continuation entry than a mean-reversion short

⏺ Here's the complete picture:

  ---
  Root cause: macro trend.

  The strategy is a short-biased momentum signal (bearish close, strong body, elevated volume). In a sustained
  bull market — when the asset is trading above its 200D SMA — every BALANCED regime pullback has an upward
  drift that stops out shorts before they reach 2R. The regime filter (BALANCED + HIGH vol) only looks at local
  structure. It can't see the macro context.

  What happened month by month:
  - 2023 Jan–May: BTC crossed above 200D SMA for the first time since early 2022 (+39% in January alone). Every
  short entry was being stopped out by the recovery drift. SL rate hit 87.8% in April 2023 — almost every single
   trade stopped out.
  - The exact same pattern hit Feb 2024 (+42.6% BTC month) and Nov 2024 (+37.2%) — both show up as the two worst
   months of 2024.

  Filter impact: asset close < 200D SMA

  ┌────────────────┬────────┬───────┬─────────┬───────┐
  │                │ Trades │ Win%  │ Total R │ MaxDD │
  ├────────────────┼────────┼───────┼─────────┼───────┤
  │ Unfiltered     │ 1,910  │ 37.7% │ +226.5  │ 39.4  │
  ├────────────────┼────────┼───────┼─────────┼───────┤
  │ Below 200D SMA │ 920    │ 39.8% │ +165.9  │ 31.9  │
  ├────────────────┼────────┼───────┼─────────┼───────┤
  │ Above 200D SMA │ 990    │ 35.9% │ +60.7   │ 34.8  │
  └────────────────┴────────┴───────┴─────────┴───────┘

  The filter cuts trades in half (1,910 → 920) but keeps 73% of the R. Win rate goes from 37.7% to 39.8%, maxDD
  drops from 39.4 to 31.9R.

  But there's a problem: ETH flips negative (-18.76R) and SOL stays weak. The filter helps most assets but isn't
   clean enough on its own. 2023 goes from -12R to -4R — better but still negative.

  The filter isn't wrong, it's insufficient. The 200D SMA is too slow — it was already above the SMA when things
   were bad. What's actually needed is: only short during local downtrends or corrective phases, not just "asset
   below 200D SMA." The 200D SMA keeps ETH/SOL filtered out during good periods too (they were below 200D in
  2023 but choppy, not cleanly trending down).

  The real fix is an additional filter: short-term trend confirmation. Before taking a short signal, confirm
  that the asset is actually in a local downswing — not just globally below a slow MA. Candidates:

  1. Price below its own 4h 50-bar SMA at signal time (50 × 4h = 200h of local trend context)
  2. Daily close making lower highs over last 5 days (structural breakdown)
  3. Both: below 200D SMA AND below 4h 50-bar SMA (dual-TF confirmation)

  Want to test that combination?

   SYMS     = ["BTCUSDT","ETHUSDT","SOLUSDT","LINKUSDT","DOGEUSDT","XRPUSDT"]

   TP_SWEEP = [1.0, 1.5, 2.0, 2.5, 3.0, 4.0]
   YEARS    = [2022, 2023, 2024, 2025]

   def max_dd(r):
       c = np.cumsum(r)
       return float(np.max(np.maximum.accumulate(c) - c)) if len(r) else 0.0

   # ── Build signals with all filter flags ───────────────────────────────────
   print("Loading and computing filters...")
   signals = []

   for sym in SYMS:
       df5 = load_merged_5m(DB, sym)
       df5 = df5.loc[df5.index >= pd.Timestamp("2022-01-01", tz="UTC")]

       # Filter 1: 4h 50-bar SMA (local trend, 200h lookback)
       df4h = resample_ohlcv(df5, "4h").copy()
       df4h["sma50_4h"] = df4h["close"].rolling(50, min_periods=25).mean()
       df4h["below_sma50_4h"] = df4h["close"] < df4h["sma50_4h"]
       # Shift 1 so bar i's SMA is known at bar i+1 entry (no lookahead)
       sma4h_series = df4h["below_sma50_4h"].shift(1).reindex(
           df5.index, method="ffill").fillna(False)

       # Filter 2: daily lower highs over last 5 days
       df1d = resample_ohlcv(df5, "1D").copy()
       # Lower high = today's high < yesterday's high, rolling 5-day window
       # "making lower highs" = ALL of last 5 days have lower highs than the day before
       lh = df1d["high"] < df1d["high"].shift(1)
       df1d["lower_highs_5d"] = lh.rolling(5, min_periods=5).sum() >= 3  # at least 3 of 5 days
       lh_series = df1d["lower_highs_5d"].shift(1).reindex(
           df5.index, method="ffill").fillna(False)

       # Filter 3: 200D SMA
       df1d["sma200d"] = df1d["close"].rolling(200, min_periods=100).mean()
       df1d["below_200d"] = df1d["close"] < df1d["sma200d"]
       sma200d_series = df1d["below_200d"].shift(1).reindex(
           df5.index, method="ffill").fillna(False)

       # Build 1h bars + regime + signal conditions
       df1h = resample_ohlcv(df5, "1h").copy()
       df1h = classify_regimes(df1h, atr_period=14, atr_ma_period=50,
                               er_period=20, er_balanced_threshold=0.35)
       rng = (df1h["high"] - df1h["low"]).replace(0, np.nan)
       df1h["close_pct"] = (df1h["close"] - df1h["low"]) / rng
       df1h["body_pct"]  = (df1h["close"] - df1h["open"]).abs() / rng
       df1h["vol_ratio"] = df1h["volume"] / df1h["volume"].rolling(20, min_periods=10).median()
       atr_r = df1h["atr_ratio"]
       p67 = atr_r.rolling(200, min_periods=50).quantile(0.67)
       p33 = atr_r.rolling(200, min_periods=50).quantile(0.33)
       vol_q = np.where(atr_r >= p67, "HIGH", np.where(atr_r < p33, "LOW", "MED")).astype(object)
       vol_q[p67.isna().values] = np.nan
       df1h["vol_q"] = vol_q

       for i in range(60, len(df1h)-1):
           row = df1h.iloc[i]
           if pd.isna(row.get("atr")) or pd.isna(row.get("vol_q")): continue
           if row["structure"] != "BALANCED": continue
           if row["vol_q"] != "HIGH": continue
           if not (row["close_pct"] < 0.20 and row["close"] < row["open"]): continue
           if not (row["vol_ratio"] > 1.5 and row["body_pct"] > 0.55): continue
           eb = df1h.iloc[i+1]
           if pd.isna(eb["open"]): continue
           ts = df1h.index[i+1]
           ep = float(eb["open"])
           atr_v = float(row["atr"])

           signals.append({
               "sym": sym, "df5": df5,
               "ts": ts, "entry_p": ep, "atr": atr_v,
               "year": ts.year,
               "f1_4h_sma":   bool(sma4h_series.get(ts, False)),
               "f2_lower_h":  bool(lh_series.get(ts, False)),
               "f3_200d":     bool(sma200d_series.get(ts, False)),
           })

   # precompute f_both = f3 AND f1
   for s in signals:
       s["f_both"] = s["f3_200d"] and s["f1_4h_sma"]

   print(f"  Total signals: {len(signals)}")
   for fname, key in [("F1 4h<SMA50","f1_4h_sma"),("F2 lower highs","f2_lower_h"),
                      ("F3 200D SMA","f3_200d"),("BOTH F1+F3","f_both")]:
       n = sum(1 for s in signals if s[key])
       print(f"  {fname}: {n} signals kept ({n/len(signals)*100:.0f}%)")

   # ── TP sweep per filter ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
   FILTERS = {
       "NO_FILTER": None,
       "F1_4h_SMA50": "f1_4h_sma",
       "F2_lower_highs": "f2_lower_h",
       "F3_200D_SMA": "f3_200d",
       "BOTH_F1+F3": "f_both",
   }

   def sweep_tp(sigs, label):
       print(f"\n{'='*80}")
       print(f"  {label}  (n_signals={len(sigs)})")
       print(f"{'='*80}")
       print(f"  {'TP':>5}  {'n':>5}  {'win%':>6}  {'avg_R':>7}  {'total_R':>8}  "
             f"{'maxDD':>7}  {'DD/n':>6}", end="")
       for yr in YEARS: print(f"  {yr}", end="")
       print()
       print("  " + "-"*85)

       rows = []
       for tp_r in TP_SWEEP:
           pnls_all, pnls_yr, pnls_sym = [], defaultdict(list), defaultdict(list)
           for s in sigs:
               ep = s["entry_p"]; stop = ep + s["atr"] * ATR_MULT
               risk = stop - ep
               if risk <= 0: continue
               tp_p = tp_price_from_r(ep, risk, -1, tp_r)
               res = replay_trade_5m(s["df5"], s["ts"], -1, ep, stop, tp_p, risk, 3.0,
                                     be_trigger_r=None, be_offset_r=0.0,
                                     skip_entry_bucket_hours=0.0)
               if res:
                   pnls_all.append(res.pnl_r)
                   pnls_yr[s["year"]].append(res.pnl_r)
                   pnls_sym[s["sym"]].append(res.pnl_r)

           r = np.array(pnls_all)
           n = len(r)
           if n == 0:
               print(f"  {tp_r:>5.1f}  no trades"); continue
           yr_tots = [round(np.array(pnls_yr.get(yr,[])).sum(),1) for yr in YEARS]
           dd = max_dd(r)
           print(f"  {tp_r:>5.1f}  {n:>5}  {(r>0).mean()*100:>6.1f}%  {r.mean():>7.4f}  "
                 f"{r.sum():>8.2f}  {dd:>7.2f}  {dd/n:>6.3f}", end="")
           for v in yr_tots: print(f"  {v:>5.1f}", end="")
           print()
           rows.append({"tp": tp_r, "n": n, "win_pct": round((r>0).mean()*100,1),
                        "total_r": round(r.sum(),2), "max_dd": round(dd,2),
                        "sym_pnl": dict(pnls_sym)})

       # Per-symbol at best TP (highest total_r)
       if rows:
           best = max(rows, key=lambda x: x["total_r"])
           print(f"\n  Best TP={best['tp']}R — per-symbol total R:")
           for sym in SYMS:
               v = round(sum(best["sym_pnl"].get(sym,[])),1)
               bar = "█"*int(abs(v)/5) if v else ""
               sign = "+" if v >= 0 else ""
               print(f"    {sym:<12} {sign}{v:>7.1f}R  {bar}")

   for fname, fkey in FILTERS.items():
       sigs = [s for s in signals if fkey is None or s[fkey]]
       sweep_tp(sigs, fname)
   EOF
   Three trend filters × TP sweep

      319 +def _add_regime_shading(fig: go.Figure, regime_slice: pd.DataFrame) -> None:                  
      320 +    """                                                                                       
      321 +    Add vertical rectangle shading behind the 4h chart based on structure.                    
      322 +    BALANCED = subtle green, IMBALANCED = subtle red.

      341 +        t1 = timestamps[j - 1] + pd.Timedelta(hours=4)  # extend to bar close                 
      342 +        color = "rgba(38,166,154,0.07)" if s == "BALANCED" else "rgba(239,83,80,0.07)"        
      343 +        fig.add_vrect(                                                                        
      344 +            x0=t0, x1=t1,                                                                     
      345 +            fillcolor=color, line_width=0,                                                    
      346 +            layer="below",                                                                    
      347 +            row=1, col=1,                                                                     
      348 +        )                                                                                     
      349 +        i = j

  shading

  regime panel axis values.

     - Distribution diagnostics: tails, skew, hit-rate by bucket.                                               
     - ATR ratio segmentation (quantiles + fixed bins) and interaction with time-of-day.                        
  3) Robustness checks:                                                                                         
     - Walk-forward splits by year (train on past, evaluate on next year).                                      
     - Bootstrap confidence intervals for win rate and avg R by key buckets.                                    
     - Multiple-testing caution: adjust interpretation for many bucket tests.

     - Propose 3–5 rule candidates that DO NOT use future information.                                          
     - Example dimensions: hour window, atr_ratio range, structure persistence, simple directional heuristic.   
     - For each candidate, define exact rule syntax and expected trade count impact.

     - Produce ranked table with: rule_name, n, win%, avg_r, total_r, max_dd_proxy, stability_score.            
     - Include a “complexity penalty” so simplest robust rules rank higher.

     - Python code (pandas/numpy) to reproduce all analyses.

⏺ Results are in. Let me compile the full picture:

  ---
  Vol regime answer:
  - In the fixed-R baseline (original run): HIGH vol slightly better (+5.62R at 1R TP, n=28)
  - In the TP-at-midband shorts sweep: LOW vol dramatically better (72.2% win, +5.20R, n=18)
  - Neither is reliable — both have n<30, which is statistically noise

  The sweeps reveal the real problem:

  Sweep A — ATR mult × TP at midband:
  The wider the stop, the better — which is the opposite of your hypothesis. Tighter stops destroy R/R because
  the midband is ~1R away regardless of stop width (it's a moving target, not a fixed level). At ATR×0.4 you
  need 18% wins just to break even on midband trades. You never get there. The midband-as-TP idea doesn't work
  because the midband drifts with price during the hold period — it's not a static target.

  Sweep B — Shorts only, TP at midband:
  Shorts are consistently better than the full pool, but still all negative. At ATR×1.5 shorts are at -39R vs
  -244R for all trades — cleaner but not profitable.

  Sweep C — Vol breakdown at ATR×1.5, shorts, TP at midband:

  ┌────────┬──────┬─────────┬───────┐
  │  Vol   │  n   │ total R │ win%  │
  ├────────┼──────┼─────────┼───────┤
  │ LOW    │ 18   │ +5.20   │ 72.2% │
  ├────────┼──────┼─────────┼───────┤
  │ HIGH   │ 27   │ -0.74   │ 40.7% │
  ├────────┼──────┼─────────┼───────┤
  │ NORMAL │ 1122 │ -43.88  │ 46.8% │
  └────────┴──────┴─────────┴───────┘

  The actual diagnosis:

  The strategy has a structural problem, not a parameter problem. On 1h XRP 2022–2026:
  - 1,122 out of 1,190 trades are NORMAL vol — that pool is reliably negative and drowns everything else
  - The long side is broken at every configuration (XRP had extended downtrends in 2022-2023 — BB longs below
  lower band are fading a trend, not reverting)
  - The BB period (20) on 1h bars produces ~2523 BALANCED signals — too many, too noisy

  The one thread worth pursuing: LOW vol BALANCED shorts with TP at midband. 72% win rate needs to be validated
  on more symbols and a wider date range before it means anything. The current n=18 could flip on a single bad
  month.

  Next 3 experiments to run:
  1. Multi-symbol LOW vol BALANCED shorts — run the same config on BTC, ETH, SOL, LINK from 2022 and check if
  the 72% win rate holds or is XRP-specific
  2. BB period sweep on 1h — test bb_period=[30, 50, 100] to reduce NORMAL-vol noise; longer bands produce fewer
   but higher-conviction signals
  3. IMBALANCED regime shorts — your trend-following intuition is probably right; BB upper band in IMBALANCED
  structure may work better as a momentum continuation entry than a mean-reversion short

  Three very clean patterns:

  1. Shorts are the entire strategy — longs are negative at every config. The short side of mom|3R is +266R; the
   long side is -73R. The long entry (strong bullish close → buy next open) is essentially fading reversals.
  2. BALANCED wins, IMBALANCED kills — BALANCED structure contributes +230R at mom|3R, IMBALANCED contributes
  -37R. Every single config shows this split. Trending markets stop out momentum entries.
  3. HIGH vol is the edge — HIGH vol thirds contribute +216R at mom|3R vs MED=-44R, LOW=+21R. The momentum close
   signal only works when the market is in an expansionary vol environment. MED vol is a drag everywhere.

  The win rate trade-off is intentional: at 3R TP, 26.6% wins is exactly what you'd need for breakeven on pure
  ATR stops (breakeven = 1/(1+tp_r) = 25%). Anything above 25% is positive expectancy at 3R — and we're getting
  26.6%, which is slim but real.

⏺ Here's the complete picture:

  ---
  Root cause: macro trend.

  The strategy is a short-biased momentum signal (bearish close, strong body, elevated volume). In a sustained
  bull market — when the asset is trading above its 200D SMA — every BALANCED regime pullback has an upward
  drift that stops out shorts before they reach 2R. The regime filter (BALANCED + HIGH vol) only looks at local
  structure. It can't see the macro context.

  What happened month by month:
  - 2023 Jan–May: BTC crossed above 200D SMA for the first time since early 2022 (+39% in January alone). Every
  short entry was being stopped out by the recovery drift. SL rate hit 87.8% in April 2023 — almost every single
   trade stopped out.
  - The exact same pattern hit Feb 2024 (+42.6% BTC month) and Nov 2024 (+37.2%) — both show up as the two worst
   months of 2024.

  Filter impact: asset close < 200D SMA

  ┌────────────────┬────────┬───────┬─────────┬───────┐
  │                │ Trades │ Win%  │ Total R │ MaxDD │
  ├────────────────┼────────┼───────┼─────────┼───────┤
  │ Unfiltered     │ 1,910  │ 37.7% │ +226.5  │ 39.4  │
  ├────────────────┼────────┼───────┼─────────┼───────┤
  │ Below 200D SMA │ 920    │ 39.8% │ +165.9  │ 31.9  │
  ├────────────────┼────────┼───────┼─────────┼───────┤
  │ Above 200D SMA │ 990    │ 35.9% │ +60.7   │ 34.8  │
  └────────────────┴────────┴───────┴─────────┴───────┘

  The filter cuts trades in half (1,910 → 920) but keeps 73% of the R. Win rate goes from 37.7% to 39.8%, maxDD
  drops from 39.4 to 31.9R.

  But there's a problem: ETH flips negative (-18.76R) and SOL stays weak. The filter helps most assets but isn't
   clean enough on its own. 2023 goes from -12R to -4R — better but still negative.

  The filter isn't wrong, it's insufficient. The 200D SMA is too slow — it was already above the SMA when things
   were bad. What's actually needed is: only short during local downtrends or corrective phases, not just "asset
   below 200D SMA." The 200D SMA keeps ETH/SOL filtered out during good periods too (they were below 200D in
  2023 but choppy, not cleanly trending down).

  The real fix is an additional filter: short-term trend confirmation. Before taking a short signal, confirm
  that the asset is actually in a local downswing — not just globally below a slow MA. Candidates:

  1. Price below its own 4h 50-bar SMA at signal time (50 × 4h = 200h of local trend context)
  2. Daily close making lower highs over last 5 days (structural breakdown)
  3. Both: below 200D SMA AND below 4h 50-bar SMA (dual-TF confirmation)

  Want to test that combination?

  - XRP should be run at a higher TP (4–5R) separately if you want to exploit its cleaner reversion

  - MIN-STOP = whichever is tighter — when FVG and OB align the stop sits at the zone boundary
  - Confluence filter = requires BOTH FVG and OB, and their zones must overlap/touch

  - Bearish OB = the last bullish candle before the displacement (the signal candle IS the displacement)
  - OB zone = body of that last bullish candle [open, close]
  - If price returns above the OB = institutional supply absorbed = short thesis dead
  - FVG + OB confluence = imbalance zone + institutional supply at same level = strongest filter

  Key ideas being tested:
  - OB-STOP = stop just above ob_high (the full OB candle's wick) — exits if price fully absorbs the sell orders
  - FVG-STOP = stop just above fvg_low — exits if the gap is filled (tightest)
  - MIN-STOP = whichever is tighter — when FVG and OB align the stop sits at the zone boundary
  - Confluence filter = requires BOTH FVG and OB, and their zones must overlap/touch

  ---                                                                                                           
  The OB Problem & What to Do Next                          
                                                                                                                
  The current OB definition (last bullish candle in prior 10 bars) is too permissive — it's always there. To
  make OB useful we need a tighter definition. Two directions worth pursuing:                                   
                                                            
  Option 1 — OB must be the candle that CREATED the FVG (bar i-1 or i-2 specifically). The OB that directly led 
  into the gap is more meaningful than a random bullish candle 8 bars ago.
                                                                                                                
  Option 2 — Institutional OB definition: the last bullish candle where the candle's close is INSIDE the FVG    
  zone (the OB delivered price INTO the gap). This is the true "smart money" confluence.
                                                                                                                
  Want me to implement one of these tighter definitions and rerun, or pivot to something else?

⏺ You're right — the current implementation has a subtle bug: when I compute risk = stop_fvg - entry, the TP    
  price also moves closer, inflating win rate artificially. The correct comparison is:                          
                                                                                                                
  - Same initial risk (ATR×mult) → same TP price for both modes                                                 
  - FVG stop is tighter → when stopped out, you exit at a smaller loss than -1R                                 
  - Win rate should be equal or slightly lower (tighter stop = hit more often on normal pullbacks)              
  - The edge comes entirely from saving R on losing trades

⏺ The study is still running. While we wait, here's what was fixed and why it matters:                          
                                                                                                                
  The bug that was in the previous run:                                                                         
                                                                                                                
  When FVG-STOP computed risk = fvg_stop - entry and used that same value for TP:                               
  - FVG-STOP risk ≈ ATR × 1.0 (tight, since fvg_low ≈ entry + ATR)                                              
  - Standard risk = ATR × 2.0                                                                                   
  - So FVG-STOP TP was at entry - 1.0×ATR×tp_r vs Standard at entry - 2.0×ATR×tp_r                              
  - FVG-STOP TP was literally half the distance — of course win rate was higher, the target was much closer     
                                                                                                                
  The previous Section C numbers (FVG-STOP 44.1% win vs STANDARD 41.4%) were entirely explained by the closer   
  TP, not by any real edge in the stop.                                                                         
                                                                                                                
  The corrected model:                                                                                          
  - Both modes use risk_basis = ATR × atr_mult — identical TP price       
  - FVG-STOP uses tighter actual stop → when stopped, exits at < -1R instead of -1R                             
  - Win rate now reflects reality: FVG-STOP may actually have lower win rate (tighter stop = hit more often on
  normal pullbacks)                                                                                             
  - The only real question is: does the R saved on losing trades outweigh any extra stop-outs?                  
                                                                                                                
  New Section C columns explain the complete picture:                                                           
  - n_sl_fvg — how many losses exited at the tighter FVG level            
  - n_sl_std — how many losses had to go all the way to the standard stop anyway                                
  - R_per_exit — average R saved each time the FVG stop fired                   
  - tot_R_saved — total benefit                                                                                 
  - saved_% — what fraction of total loss burden was offset

  Option 1 (FVG Creator): For a bearish FVG at bar i, high[i] < low[i-2]. Bar i-2 is literally the candle whose 
  low forms the FVG top. If bar i-2 is bullish → it's the OB that set up the entire FVG.

  "delivered" price into the zone. The gap now exists exactly where that candle left off.                       
                                                                                                                
  Also adding a third stop mode this unlocks: FVG-HIGH stop (fvg_high + buf = exits if price re-enters the whole
   FVG zone, OB body bottom), which sits between FVG-LOW and standard.

⏺ Good catch. The 4.2R baseline was from the standard stop studies (study_order_blocks / study_ob_strict). The 6.0R in the new study uses the       
  FVG-LOW stop, which changes the TP landscape.                                                                                                     
                                                                                                                                                    
  Let me show you the exact 1h numbers at 4.25R from the new run versus 6.0R:                                                                       
                                                                                                                                                    
  From the Section A output:                                                                                                                        
  4.25R   226   29.6%   0.6295   142.3   10.3   0.045   11   33.2
   4.5R   225   27.1%   0.5637   126.8   12.9   0.057   11   29.6  ← cliff                                                                          
   ...                                                                                                                                              
   6.0R   225   23.1%   0.6882   154.8   14.0   0.062   14   36.2                                                                                   
                                                                                                                                                    
  The auto-filter ranked 6.0R #1 because DD/n=0.062 still passes the < 0.08 threshold and the annualized return is slightly higher (36.2 vs 33.2).  
  But there's still a real cliff at 4.5R — DD jumps from 10.3 → 12.9 and win% drops from 29.6% → 27.1%.                                             
                                                                                                                                                    
  The difference from 4.2R:                                                                                                                         
                                                            
  - 4.2R was standard stop optimal: When you use the full ATR×2 stop, every loss is a full -1R. TP at 4.2R was the best return-to-DD tradeoff.      
  - With FVG-LOW stop, losses are cut smaller (< -1R when the FVG is touched first), so the cumulative R improves at higher TPs without
  proportionally more DD.                                                                                                                           
                                                            
  The cross-HTF summary is misleading because it reports candidates[0] = 6.0R. The more apples-to-apples comparison to the 4.2R baseline is 4.25R   
  with FVG-LOW = 33.2R/yr, 10.3 maxDD, vs old 4.2R standard = ~25-31R/yr.

  ---                                                                                                                                               
  MFE Lock Sweep Results                                                                                                                            
                                                                                                                                                    
  Baseline: FVG-LOW no lock, TP=4.25R → 29.6% win, 142.3R, maxDD=10.3, 33.2R/yr                                                                     
                                                                                                                                                    
  Key finding: every lock config loses R vs the no-lock baseline. The best single-stage is mfe=2.5R → BE at 130.2R (Δ-12.1R). The best two-stage is 
  [(2.5R→BE), (3.0R→0.25R)] at 134.9R (Δ-7.4R).                                                                                                     
                            
  Why: at 29.6% win rate with TP=4.25R, about 26% of trades actually reach 2.5R before TP. Locking those at BE converts a trade that would have     
  eventually hit TP into a break-even. More trades get clipped at the lock than get saved from a reversal.
                                                
  The breakdown tells the story:                                                                                                                    
  - SL% stays at 62.8% (same FVG-LOW fires regardless of lock)
  - BE% = 10.6% with 2.5R lock — those ~24 trades hit 2.5R, locked, then reversed past entry                                                        
  - TP% drops from 29.6% → 26.5% — you lose ~7 TP hits that got sniped at the lock level    
                                                                                                                                                    
  The only year that benefits is 2024 (+7.1R) — a ranging/choppy year where winners that run toward TP then reverse. But 2022 (-5.5R), 2023 (-3.1R) 
  lose because those winning trades had clean momentum and ran all the way.                                                                         
                                                
  Conclusion: The 4.25R TP with the FVG-LOW stop is already the right architecture. Adding an MFE lock doesn't help this strategy — the best trades 
  run clean to TP. The FVG-LOW stop is doing the job of cutting losers early; a profit lock on top of that doesn't add edge.

⏺ Results are interesting — let me walk through what we found.                                                                                      
                                                            
  ---                                                                                                                                               
  Reversal-at-TP Results                                                                                                                            
                                                                                                                                                    
  The geometry is extreme. Every reversal TP is ≥15R because:                                                                                       
  - Short drops 4.25R × ATR×2.0 = 8.5 ATRs                                                                                                          
  - FVG gap (fvg_low) is slightly above original entry (~10+ ATRs above reversal entry)                                                             
  - Median implied TP = 10.15 ATR → at SL×0.25 that's ~40R per trade                                                                                
                                                                                                                                                    
  The SL sweep story:                                                                                                                               
                                                                                                                                                    
  ┌─────────┬─────┬────────┬────────┬──────────┬───────┬──────┐                                                                                     
  │ SL mult │  n  │  win%  │ impl_R │ total_R  │ maxDD │ DD/n │
  ├─────────┼─────┼────────┼────────┼──────────┼───────┼──────┤                                                                                     
  │ ×0.25   │ 66  │ 4.5%   │ 40R    │ 56.1R    │ 34.6  │ 0.52 │
  ├─────────┼─────┼────────┼────────┼──────────┼───────┼──────┤
  │ ×1.0    │ 66  │ 10.6%  │ 10R    │ 12.3R    │ 18.9  │ 0.29 │                                                                                     
  ├─────────┼─────┼────────┼────────┼──────────┼───────┼──────┤                                                                                     
  │ ×1.25   │ 66  │ 13.6%  │ 8R     │ 16.5R    │ 17.4  │ 0.26 │                                                                                     
  ├─────────┼─────┼────────┼────────┼──────────┼───────┼──────┤                                                                                     
  │ ×2.0+   │ 66  │ 15-26% │ 3-5R   │ negative │ —     │ —    │
  └─────────┴─────┴────────┴────────┴──────────┴───────┴──────┘                                                                                     
                                                            
  Critical finding: once SL ≥ 2.0 ATR the strategy goes negative. The win rate doesn't grow fast enough to overcome the larger losses. Only the very
   tight SL levels (×0.25, ×0.5) produce positive total_R because the rare wins (1 in 22 trades at ×0.25) each return ~40R.
                                                                                                                                                    
  The combined picture looks good on paper (198.4R, 46.3R/yr) but the reversal contribution has maxDD=34.6 — 3.3× the short's maxDD. The reversal is
   essentially a lottery: 20 losses in a row, then one 40R winner.
                                                                                                                                                    
  Year breakdown confirms the problem: 2023 and 2024 had zero reversal wins. BTC and LINK had zero wins at any SL. The 56R is driven by ETHUSDT     
  (+37.5R) and XRPUSDT (+33.4R) in specific years.
                                                                                                                                                    
  Verdict: The FVG fill after a 4.25R short drop is a very low-probability event (~4.5% at tight SL). The math works on ×0.25 because 40R × 4.5% >  
  1R × 95.5%, but the 34.6R maxDD and zero-win years make it non-tradeable in practice. The original short-only config (33.2R/yr, maxDD=10.3) is far
   more consistent.

❯ is there anything as far as reversals we can do into this strategy or should we look for a new one                                                
                                                                                                     
⏺ Looking at the data honestly:                                                                                                                     
                                                            
  Why reversals don't work here structurally:                                                                                                       
  - The short TP is 8.5 ATRs below entry. The FVG is 10+ ATRs away from there. Any reversal TP near the FVG is a lottery.
  - At tighter SLs the R-multiple is ~40R which means even a "good" 4.5% win rate barely makes money and has 34R maxDD — three times the short      
  strategy's DD.                                                                                                                              
  - 2023 and 2024 had zero reversal wins. BTC and LINK had zero wins across the entire 3-year period.                                               
                                                                                                     
  The one reversal that might be worth testing — SL-hit reversal:                                                                                   
  When the FVG-LOW stop fires (price rallied back to fill the FVG bottom), that IS a FVG reclaim. You could enter long at the SL exit with a short  
  TP like 1R–2R (not trying to run the full gap). The SL-hit is 70.4% of trades (159 cases), much better sample size. But I'd expect marginal       
  results since the same BALANCED+HIGH signal that triggered the short is now reversed.                                                             
                                                                                                                                                    
  For a genuinely new direction, these have the most potential given what we know:                                                                  
   
  1. Symmetrical long — same filter flipped: BALANCED + HIGH vol + bullish candle + close near HIGH + FVG above. The signal structure already found 
  strong mean-reversion on shorts; longs in the same regime should have comparable characteristics. This doubles signal count.
  2. Imbalanced regime trend-follow — we've only traded BALANCED (choppy). The signals we're filtering OUT (IMBALANCED) might work well with a      
  trend-following approach — wider TP, tighter SL, no FVG filter.                                                                                   
  3. FVG retest entry — instead of entering at signal bar i+1, wait for price to retrace into the FVG zone before entering. Lower frequency but
  potentially higher win rate since you're entering at proven supply rather than immediately after the displacement.                                
                                                            
  Which direction interests you most?

   import sys, numpy as np; sys.path.insert(0,'.')                                                                                                  
   from lab.study_fvg_momentum import prepare_sym, DEFAULT_DB, SYMS                                                                                 
   import pandas as pd                                                                                                                              
                                                                                                                                                    
   # Quick signal count across all symbols for IMBALANCED+HIGH                                                                                      
   all_counts = {}                                                                                                                                  
   for sym in SYMS:                                                                                                                                 
       df5, df1h = prepare_sym(DEFAULT_DB, sym, '2022-01-01')                                                                                       
       df = df1h.dropna(subset=['structure','vol_q','atr'])                                                                                         
       imb_high = df[(df['structure']=='IMBALANCED') & (df['vol_q']=='HIGH')]                                                                       
                                                                                                                                                    
       rng = (imb_high['high'] - imb_high['low']).replace(0, np.nan)                                                                                
       close_pct = (imb_high['close'] - imb_high['low']) / rng                                                                                      
       body_pct  = (imb_high['close'] - imb_high['open']).abs() / rng                                                                               
       vol_ratio = imb_high['volume'] / imb_high['volume'].rolling(20, min_periods=10).mean()                                                       

       bears = imb_high[
           (imb_high['close'] < imb_high['open']) &
           (body_pct > 0.55) &
           (close_pct < 0.15) &
           (imb_high['volume'] / df['volume'].rolling(20,min_periods=10).median().reindex(imb_high.index) > 1.8)
       ]
       bulls = imb_high[
           (imb_high['close'] > imb_high['open']) &
           (body_pct > 0.55) &
           (close_pct > 0.85) &
           (imb_high['volume'] / df['volume'].rolling(20,min_periods=10).median().reindex(imb_high.index) > 1.8)
       ]
       all_counts[sym] = {'imb_high': len(imb_high), 'bears': len(bears), 'bulls': len(bulls)}
       print(f'{sym:<12} imb_high={len(imb_high):>4}  bears={len(bears):>3}  bulls={len(bulls):>3}')

   totals = {k: sum(v[k] for v in all_counts.values()) for k in ['imb_high','bears','bulls']}
   print(f'  TOTAL       imb_high={totals[\"imb_high\"]:>4}  bears={totals[\"bears\"]:>3}  bulls={totals[\"bulls\"]:>3}')

  ---
  MFE Lock Sweep Results

  Baseline: FVG-LOW no lock, TP=4.25R → 29.6% win, 142.3R, maxDD=10.3, 33.2R/yr

  Key finding: every lock config loses R vs the no-lock baseline. The best single-stage is mfe=2.5R → BE at 130.2R (Δ-12.1R). The best two-stage is
  [(2.5R→BE), (3.0R→0.25R)] at 134.9R (Δ-7.4R).

  Why: at 29.6% win rate with TP=4.25R, about 26% of trades actually reach 2.5R before TP. Locking those at BE converts a trade that would have
  eventually hit TP into a break-even. More trades get clipped at the lock than get saved from a reversal.

  The breakdown tells the story:
  - SL% stays at 62.8% (same FVG-LOW fires regardless of lock)
  - BE% = 10.6% with 2.5R lock — those ~24 trades hit 2.5R, locked, then reversed past entry
  - TP% drops from 29.6% → 26.5% — you lose ~7 TP hits that got sniped at the lock level

  The only year that benefits is 2024 (+7.1R) — a ranging/choppy year where winners that run toward TP then reverse. But 2022 (-5.5R), 2023 (-3.1R)
  lose because those winning trades had clean momentum and ran all the way.

  Conclusion: The 4.25R TP with the FVG-LOW stop is already the right architecture. Adding an MFE lock doesn't help this strategy — the best trades
  run clean to TP. The FVG-LOW stop is doing the job of cutting losers early; a profit lock on top of that doesn't add edge.
