⏺ Both issues investigated. Here's what I found:                                                                                                                          
                                                                                                                                                                          
  ---                                                                                                                                                                     
  Issue 1 — S3: The FVG-LOW stop at TP=4.25R was real and was better                                                                                                      
                                                                                                                                                                          
  The config lives in study_fvg_lock_sweep.py. The baseline was confirmed:                                                                                                
                                                                                                                                                                          
  ┌───────────────────────────┬───────────┬───────┬───────┬────────┐                                                                                                      
  │          Config           │ n signals │ ann_R │ maxDD │ Calmar │                                                                                                      
  ├───────────────────────────┼───────────┼───────┼───────┼────────┤                                                                                                      
  │ S3 FVG-LOW stop, TP=4.25R │ 226       │ 33.2  │ 10.3  │ 3.22   │                                                                                                      
  ├───────────────────────────┼───────────┼───────┼───────┼────────┤
  │ S3 ATR stop, TP=4.5R      │ 631       │ 35.6  │ 27.5  │ 1.29   │                                                                                                      
  ├───────────────────────────┼───────────┼───────┼───────┼────────┤                                                                                                      
  │ S3 ATR stop, TP=5.0R      │ 631       │ 37.0  │ 33.0  │ 1.12   │                                                                                                      
  └───────────────────────────┴───────────┴───────┴───────┴────────┘                                                                                                      
                                                                                                                                                                          
  The FVG-LOW stop version has 3× better maxDD (10.3 vs 33.0) at nearly identical ann_R. Calmar goes from 1.12 to 3.22. The cost: 226 vs 631 signals — only FVG-tagged    
  bars qualify (bearish gap must exist: high[i] < low[i-2]).                                                                                                              
                                                                                                                                                                          
  The stop mechanics: stop = fvg_low + ATR×0.15 = high[i] + ATR×0.15. If price rallies back up to fill the FVG gap, the short thesis is structurally invalid — so you exit
   small rather than holding to full -ATR×2 stop. That's why the DD is so much tighter.                                                                                   
                                                                                                                                                                          
  Best lock on top of FVG-LOW stop (single stage):                                                                                                                        
                                                     
  ┌───────────────────┬───────┬───────┬────────┐                                                                                                                          
  │      Stages       │ ann_R │ maxDD │ Calmar │    
  ├───────────────────┼───────┼───────┼────────┤                                                                                                                          
  │ No lock baseline  │ 33.2  │ 10.3  │ 3.22   │
  ├───────────────────┼───────┼───────┼────────┤
  │ mfe=2.5R → BE     │ 30.4  │ 10.3  │ 2.95   │
  ├───────────────────┼───────┼───────┼────────┤                                                                                                                          
  │ mfe=3.0R → +0.25R │ 30.4  │ 10.8  │ 2.81   │    
  └───────────────────┴───────┴───────┴────────┘                                                                                                                          
                                                    
  The lock doesn't improve on the no-lock FVG baseline much — the FVG stop is already tight enough. S3 should be: FVG-only signals, FVG-LOW stop, TP=4.25R, no additional 
  lock.                                             
                                                                                                                                                                          
  ---                          
  Issue 2 — S1: The MFE ladder IS valid, but here are the actual stages
                                                                                                                                                                          
  The confirmed run used 3-stage ladder with these exact defaults:
                                                                                                                                                                          
  Stage 1:  mfe=1.0R  → lock=0.8R   (gap: 0.2R)     
  Stage 2:  mfe=6.5R  → lock=5.5R   (gap: 1.0R)                                                                                                                           
  Stage 3:  mfe=10.0R → lock=9.0R   (gap: 1.0R)     
                                                                                                                                                                          
  cap_lock_by_mfe=True on all stages. MFE > lock at every stage — the engine is valid.                                                                                    
                                                    
  The user concern about "lock=3R when MFE=3R" does not apply to this config. What you described would be like (3.0, 3.0) — with cap_lock_by_mfe=True, lock_eff = min(3.0,
   3.0) = 3.0, meaning the stop lands exactly at current price. That would effectively be a take-profit-at-3R, not a trailing stop. That bug exists in the engine as a
  possibility but these stages avoid it.                                                                                                                                  
                               
  What the actual stages mean in plain English:
  - When trade reaches +1R gain → stop jumps to +0.8R (near-BE protection, very early)
  - When trade reaches +6.5R → stop jumps to +5.5R                                                                                                                        
  - When trade reaches +10R → stop jumps to +9R     
  - TP at 13R is the hard exit if price doesn't retrace                                                                                                                   
                                                       
  The stage 1 gap of only 0.2R is tight — a trade that reaches 1R on a bar's high but has a low that's 0.2R below the trigger will immediately exit at 0.8R. In practice  
  this fires often on volatile 5m bars. That's the tradeoff being made: protect against reversals early at the cost of some winners being forced out at +0.8R instead of  
  running to 13R.

  ---
  What the mechanism does

  At MFE=3R, stop moves to entry +1R (small locked profit) and then price runs free to TP=19.5R. This converts all trades that reach 3R but reverse back into small wins
  instead of full −1R stops.

  - MCL drops from 29 → 11 — losing streak cut by 62%
  - maxDD drops from 29.5 → 16.3 — drawdown nearly halved
  - win% jumps from 11.7% → 31.4% — much easier to follow psychologically

  The ann_R drops (88→57) because some trades that would have run to 19.5R now exit at +1R when price reverses after the trigger. That's the cost.

  ---
  Year Breakdown — best config (3R→+1R, TP=19.5R)

  ┌──────┬──────────────────────┐
  │ Year │        ann_R         │
  ├──────┼──────────────────────┤
  │ 2022 │ −1.2 ← only bad year │
  ├──────┼──────────────────────┤
  │ 2023 │ +29.4                │
  ├──────┼──────────────────────┤
  │ 2024 │ +23.1                │
  ├──────┼──────────────────────┤
  │ 2025 │ +6.3                 │
  └──────┴──────────────────────┘

  ---
  Sizing insight

  Because maxDD is halved (16.3 vs 29.5), this config can be sized ~1.5× larger for the same absolute drawdown budget:
  - 57.2 × 1.5 = 85.8 effective ann_R vs 88.1 baseline, but with 24.5 DD vs 29.5

  That makes the locked version strictly better on a risk-adjusted basis once you account for position sizing.

  ---
  Ladders underperform the simple trigger

  The MFE ladder complexity doesn't pay off here. The best ladder (3→0, 6→3, 10→7, 15→11) gets Calmar=2.64 — worse than the simple 3R→+1R at 3.51. Reason: the ladder's
  intermediate lock stages (locking at +3R when at 6R, etc.) prematurely exit trades that would have gone to 19.5R and recovered the locked portion.

  ---
  Where to go from here

  Two natural next steps:

  1. Fine-tune the trigger — scan trig=2.5–4R, lock=0.5–2R at TP=19.5R to find if 3R/+1R is truly optimal or if nearby configs are better
  2. 2022 fix — that small −1.2 loss comes from low signal count (41 trades, 22% win). Explore whether adding a 4H trend filter (e.g. price above 20-period MA) gates out
  the choppy 2022 environment

  Want to do the fine-tune trigger sweep or explore the 2022 filter first?

⏺ Now I have the full picture. Here's the complete breakdown:

  ---
  Which one uses the FVG stop?

  None of the 4 live streams use it as their primary stop. The FVG stop exists in study_imbalanced_trend.py as an optional variant (--fvg flag) and was researched in
  study_fvg_momentum.py, but it was not selected for live deployment — sample sizes were small (44 FVG signals in BAL+HIGH short) and the ATR stop won in testing.

  ---
  The 4 Strategies Explained

  ---
  S1 — IMBAL+HIGH Long

  "Trending market, ride the wave"

  The market is classified as IMBALANCED when the Efficiency Ratio (ER) ≥ 0.35 — price is moving directionally, not randomly. HIGH vol means there's real force behind the
   move. When those two conditions align and a strong bullish candle forms (body > 55% of range, close in top 15%), you buy the next bar's open and assume the trend
  continues.

  - Stop: entry − ATR×2 (below the candle's volatility range)
  - Management: MFE ladder lock — at 3R of favorable move, stop locks in at +3R. Trades that go far get protected.
  - TP: 13R
  - Why it works: In a real trend, momentum candles resolve forward, not backward. The ATR stop is far enough that noise doesn't shake you out.

  ---
  S2 — BAL+HIGH Short

  "Exhaustion spike in a ranging market"

  The market is BALANCED (ER < 0.35) — it's cycling, not trending. HIGH vol means a big candle just fired. When a strong bearish candle appears in a ranging market
  (vol_ratio > 1.5, body > 55%, close near the low), it's likely an exhaustion spike — the market overshot and will snap back.

  - Stop: entry + ATR×1.5 (above the spike's range)
  - TP: 3R (ranging markets mean-revert quickly, don't need a big target)
  - Why it works: In a ranging market, big directional candles are overreactions. The regime filter (BALANCED) is the key — the same candle in an IMBALANCED market is a
  trend signal (S3), not a reversal.

  ---
  S3 — IMBAL+HIGH Short

  "Trending market, ride the wave down"

  Mirror image of S1. IMBALANCED+HIGH + strong bearish candle. Market is in a downtrend with force, so sell the momentum.

  - Stop: entry + ATR×2 (above the candle, standard)
  - TP: 5R (shorter than S1's 13R — trending shorts in crypto historically resolve faster than longs)
  - Why it works: Same thesis as S1 flipped. When structure is bearish trending, bearish candles continue.

  ---
  S4 — BAL+HIGH Swing Low Long ← NEW

  "Stop hunt trap — buy the fake breakdown"

  Finds two swing lows within 0.5% of each other (equal lows = visible support everyone can see). When price dips below that level but closes back above it in the same 1h
   candle — and the close is in the top 10% of the bar's range (near-perfect V-shape) — institutions absorbed the panic sell orders and are now pushing price up.

  - Stop: entry − ATR×2
  - Management: At MFE=3.5R, stop moves to entry+1R (locks a small win). Trade then runs free to TP or exits at +1R if it reverses.
  - TP: 19.5R — the few that run, run far
  - Why it works: The equal-lows level is where retail places stops. Institutions sweep those stops to acquire liquidity, then reverse. The BAL+HIGH filter ensures the
  sweep happens in a volatile-but-ranging environment where reversals are sharp.

  ---
  The FVG Stop — what it would do

  In study_imbalanced_trend.py, the FVG stop logic exists for both shorts and longs:

  - Short FVG stop: stop = high[signal_bar] + ATR×0.15 — the signal bar left a bearish gap (high[i] < low[i-2]), meaning price skipped over a zone. If price rallies back
  up to fill that gap, the short thesis is wrong → exit early for a smaller loss than the full ATR stop.
  - Long FVG stop: stop = low[signal_bar] − ATR×0.15 — bullish gap left behind, stop below the gap floor.

  It was tested and didn't beat ATR stop in the IMBAL+HIGH regime — the trend had enough momentum that waiting for gap-fill was causing premature exits on winners.

  bars qualify (bearish gap must exist: high[i] < low[i-2]).

  The stop mechanics: stop = fvg_low + ATR×0.15 = high[i] + ATR×0.15. If price rallies back up to fill the FVG gap, the short thesis is structurally invalid — so you exit
   small rather than holding to full -ATR×2 stop. That's why the DD is so much tighter.

  Best lock on top of FVG-LOW stop (single stage):

  ┌───────────────────┬───────┬───────┬────────┐
  │      Stages       │ ann_R │ maxDD │ Calmar │

  └───────────────────┴───────┴───────┴────────┘

  The lock doesn't improve on the no-lock FVG baseline much — the FVG stop is already tight enough. S3 should be: FVG-only signals, FVG-LOW stop, TP=4.25R, no additional
  lock.

  ---
  Issue 2 — S1: The MFE ladder IS valid, but here are the actual stages

  The confirmed run used 3-stage ladder with these exact defaults:

  Stage 1:  mfe=1.0R  → lock=0.8R   (gap: 0.2R)
  Stage 2:  mfe=6.5R  → lock=5.5R   (gap: 1.0R)
  Stage 3:  mfe=10.0R → lock=9.0R   (gap: 1.0R)

  cap_lock_by_mfe=True on all stages. MFE > lock at every stage — the engine is valid.

  The user concern about "lock=3R when MFE=3R" does not apply to this config. What you described would be like (3.0, 3.0) — with cap_lock_by_mfe=True, lock_eff = min(3.0,
   3.0) = 3.0, meaning the stop lands exactly at current price. That would effectively be a take-profit-at-3R, not a trailing stop. That bug exists in the engine as a
  possibility but these stages avoid it.

  What the actual stages mean in plain English:
  - When trade reaches +1R gain → stop jumps to +0.8R (near-BE protection, very early)
  - When trade reaches +6.5R → stop jumps to +5.5R
  - When trade reaches +10R → stop jumps to +9R
  - TP at 13R is the hard exit if price doesn't retrace

  The stage 1 gap of only 0.2R is tight — a trade that reaches 1R on a bar's high but has a low that's 0.2R below the trigger will immediately exit at 0.8R. In practice
  this fires often on volatile 5m bars. That's the tradeoff being made: protect against reversals early at the cost of some winners being forced out at +0.8R instead of
  running to 13R.
